## Role
Pay-api's JSON Schema (draft-07) library for the BC Registries pay system: request/response schemas under `pay-api/src/pay_api/schemas/schemas/*.json`, plus `schemas/utils.py`, which loads them and validates payloads. It makes no calls to other services. Pay-api code validates incoming and outgoing payloads against it. Schemas reference each other by `$id` URL (`https://bcrs.gov.bc.ca/.well_known/schemas/<name>`).

Unrelated side note: the notes also contain a `payment_receipt_input.json` entry, which is only a placeholder reply with no content.

## Contract
- In: `validate(json_data, schema_id, schema_store, validate_schema, schema_search_path)` returns `(True, None)` or `(False, errors)`. The schema id is `{BASE_URI}/{schema_id}`, with `BASE_URI = 'https://bcrs.gov.bc.ca/.well_known/schemas'`.
- Out: `get_schema(filename)` returns a schema dict. `serialize(errors)` returns a list of `.message` strings.
- Key shapes:
  - `payment_request`: requires `businessInfo` and `filingInfo`; optional `paymentInfo`, `accountInfo`, `details`.
  - `business_info`: requires `corpType`.
  - `filing_info`: requires `filingTypes` with at least 1 item; `date` pattern `YYYY-M-D`.
  - `filing_type`: requires `filingTypeCode`.
  - `invoice`, `invoices` (`items`), `transaction`, `transactions`, `transaction_request` (requires `clientSystemUrl` and `payReturnUrl`).
  - `routing_slip`, `routing_slip_link_request`, `routing_slip_search_request`.
  - `payment` (requires `paymentMethod` and `paidAmount`).
  - `refund`, `refund_routing_slip`, `refund_shortname`, `eft_payment`, `eft_short_name`.
  - `statement_notification_request`, `recipients`, `purchase_history_request` (date, week and month filters).
  - `error` and `problem`.

## Decisions and checks
- `get_schema_store`: loads every `.json` file with an `$id` into a dict keyed by `$id`. With `validate_schema=True` it calls `Draft7Validator.check_schema` on each file.
- `validate`: builds the store if none is passed. It returns `(True, None)` if `is_valid()`, otherwise `(False, iter_errors())`.
- `payment.json`: `paymentMethod` must be one of EFT, WIRE, REFUND, DRAWDOWN, CASH, CHEQUE.
- `eft_payment.json`: `action` is CANCEL or APPLY_CREDITS.
- `payment_info.json`: `methodOfPayment` is one of CC, DRAWDOWN, DIRECT_PAY, ONLINE_BANKING, PAD, EFT, WIRE, EJV.
- `routing_slip.json`: `number` must be exactly 9 digits (`^([\d]+)$`, min and max length 9).
- `routing_slip_search_request.json`: `target` is `routing_slip_date` or `created_on`.
- `recipients.json`: all four fields required, `additionalProperties: false`, email regex.
- `statement_notification_request.json`: `accountName` pattern `^[^\s]+(\s+[^\s]+)*$`; no extra properties.
- `eft_short_name.json`: `casSupplierNumber` max 25 chars, `email` max 100 chars.
- `business_info.json`: `businessIdentifier` is 1–20 chars.
- `filing_info.json`: `filingIdentifier` and `folioNumber` are max 50 chars.

## Boundaries
- Entry points (`get_schema`, `get_schema_store`, `validate`, `serialize`) have no authorization guard.
- `validate` catches `SchemaError` and returns `(False, error)`. `get_schema_store` re-raises `SchemaError` and `JSONDecodeError`.
- The code has no retry or logging, and it calls no external service. It only does file I/O and uses the jsonschema `RefResolver`.
- `filing_type.json` marks `waiveFees` "Only for staff users", but the schema has no check for that. Any staff-only rule must be enforced elsewhere.
- Many fields accept any string (`^(.*)$`), including statuses, dates and URLs.
- No enum constraints on `statusCode` or `refundType`.
- `refund_shortname.json` has no email format check.

## Hazards
- Schemas are loose: no required lists, ranges or enums on many fields. Bad values pass validation.
- `line_item.json` and `invoice.json` have type mismatches. Defaults are 0 on string fields, and money fields are integers in `line_item.json`.
- `get_schema_store` only validates the schemas themselves when `validate_schema=True`. A malformed schema, such as the `payment_info.json` copy where `revenueAccount` sits outside `properties`, can pass silently otherwise.

## Open first
1. `pay-api/src/pay_api/schemas/utils.py`: loader and validator.
2. `schemas/payment_request.json`: top-level request and its refs (`payment_info`, `business_info`, `filing_info`, `account_info`, `invoice_details`).
3. `schemas/routing_slip.json` and `schemas/payment.json`: stricter rules.
4. `schemas/purchase_history_request.json`: search filters.

## Connections
- [L1] auth-api `payment_info.json`: a same-named schema in auth-api, with the same `paymentMethod` enum and a `revenueAccount` that refs `distribution_code`. The auth-api copy puts `revenueAccount` outside `properties`, so it is not applied as a property rule there.
- [L8]/[L9] pay-api models: the `transaction` schema is the item type for `transactions.json` `items`. The notes show no check on the model side.
- [L11]/[L12] `models/invoice.py` and `models/payment.py`: these produce invoices and filter on the same fields as `invoice.json` and `purchase_history_request.json`.
  - `_clean_up` and `from_row` map `PAID` to `COMPLETED`, which the status-code-as-any-string schema does not constrain.
  - `filter_date` reads `dateFilter`, `weekFilter` and `monthFilter`. `filter_details` reads `lineItems`, `details` and `lineItemsAndDetails`.
  - `lineItemsAndDetails` is handled in the model, but the notes show no matching property in the schema excerpts.
- [L4], [L5], [L6], [L7] (payment-jobs tasks) use `InvoiceReference` models. They do not use the JSON schema, though the `invoice_reference.json` fields mirror it.

**future-effective-filings** is a one-shot batch job. It asks the legal API for filings whose effective date has arrived, then publishes each filing id to the entity-filer NATS queue.

Note: the MCP servers claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive need authorization in the claude.ai connector settings. They are unavailable until then. This did not affect this summary.

## Contract
- **Takes from:** legal API `GET {LEGAL_API_URL}/internal/filings/future_effective`, sent with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The code treats the response as a list of filing ids.
- **Token:** `requests.post` to `ACCOUNT_SVC_AUTH_URL` with basic auth `(ACCOUNT_SVC_CLIENT_ID, ACCOUNT_SVC_CLIENT_SECRET)` and data `grant_type=client_credentials`.
- **Hands to:** `queue_service.publish(subject, msg)` with `subject = os.getenv('NATS_FILER_SUBJECT', '')` and `msg = {'filing': {'id': filing_id}}`. The consumer is the entity-filer worker. The job writes no state of its own.

## Decisions (`file_future_effective.py`)
- `run()`: if `filing_ids` is falsy, it logs 'No filings found to apply.' and skips the loop.
- `get_filing_ids()`: if `response.status_code != 200`, it raises an Exception.
- `get_bearer_token()`: any exception is caught and `None` is returned.
- `create_app()`: if `SENTRY_DSN` is truthy, Sentry is initialised.
- `config.py` `get_named_config`: production, staging and default give ProdConfig. testing gives TestConfig. development gives DevConfig. Any other name raises KeyError.
- `_Config`: a SENTRY_DSN of 'null' becomes ''.
- Makefile `cd`: TAG_NAME=test tags the image to test. TAG_NAME=prod tags the previous prod as prod-YYYY-MM-DD, then tags test as prod. Anything else defaults to dev and runs `build` then `tag`.

## Boundaries
- **Entry points:** `run()`, `get_filing_ids()`, `get_bearer_token()` and `create_app()` have no guard. The container CMD runs `python /opt/app-root/file_future_effective.py`. The job runs as non-root user 1001.
- **Publishing:** each publish is independent, with no transaction or rollback. `run()` catches every exception in the filing loop, logs it with `application.logger.error` and continues. The top-level `__main__` logs and re-raises.
- **Failed token fetch:** `None` is returned, so the GET goes out with `Bearer None`. It then fails the non-200 check, but the original cause is hidden.
- **Build and push:** the Makefile `push` runs docker login to `OPENSHIFT_DOCKER_REGISTRY` as `OPENSHIFT_SA_NAME` with `OPENSHIFT_SA_TOKEN`. It then pushes `REGISTRY_IMAGE:latest`. `oc` tagging needs `OPENSHIFT_REPOSITORY` and the other OpenShift variables. There is no error handling or retry.
- **Build template:** `k8s/templates/bc.yaml` builds with `pullSecret artifactory-creds` and `runPolicy: Serial`.
- **Mismatch:** the template's Dockerfile runs `future_effective_filings.py`, while the repo Dockerfile runs `file_future_effective.py`. Which one applies depends on the build path.
- **Missing:** no health checks and no retry on API or publish failures.
- **Credentials:** `devops/vaults.json` maps vault `shared` to nats, and vault `entity` to filings-jobs, nats-filer, entity-service-account and sentry.

## Hazards
1. There is no duplicate guard. If the job runs again before the filer processes the ids, the same filing id is published twice.
2. A failed publish is only logged and never retried, so that filing is skipped until the next run.
3. `NATS_FILER_SUBJECT` defaults to '' in the job. If the variable is unset, publishing goes to an empty subject without a clear error. The job's `config.py` defaults it to `entity.filing.filer`, but `file_future_effective.py` reads `os.getenv` directly.

## Open first
- `file_future_effective.py`: all job logic (token, fetch, publish).
- `config.py`: NATS, account-service and legal API settings.
- `Makefile`: build, push and tag flow.
- `Dockerfile`: runtime entry.

## Connections
- **[L3] entity-filer `config.py`:** the filer reads `NATS_FILER_SUBJECT` and `NATS_QUEUE`, both defaulting to 'error' there. This job publishes to its own `NATS_FILER_SUBJECT`. If the two are not set to the same value, messages land on a subject the filer is not subscribed to. The notes show no check on either side.
- **[L1] legal-api `reviews.py`:** POST /reviews/<id> publishes to `NATS_FILER_SUBJECT` when `filing.status == APPROVED` and `effective_date <= now`. This job covers future-effective filings by the same subject. Both send filing ids, so a filing could be queued by both paths. The notes show no duplicate guard.
- **[L2] business-pay `queue.py`:** it is a separate NATS/STAN publisher. It shares only the subject variable name and does not shape this job.

linked.label: L1
linked.why: Another publisher to the same filer subject; duplicate risk

linked.label: L2
linked.why: Only shares a name; different publisher

linked.label: L3
linked.why: Filer consumer config; subject must match

structured.brief:
## Role
Front-end filing UI (Vue, `src/views`, `src/components/EntityInfo`, `src/assets`). It collects filing data, saves or files it through `LegalServices` (create, update, fetch, `hasPendingTasks`), then sends the user to the pay UI (`getAuthWebUrl + 'makepayment/' + paymentToken + '/' + encodeURIComponent(baseUrl + '?filing_id=' + filingId)`) or back to the business dashboard. The notes show no credential on these calls. `src/assets` holds SCSS and the BC Sans font (OFL licence); they hold no logic.

## Contract
- In: route query `filing_id` (0 = new, >0 = resume draft, NaN = invalid), store getters (`getIdentifier`, `getLegalName`, `getLegalType`, `isRoleStaff`, `isAllowed(AllowableActions.*)`), feature flags.
- Out, filing payload `{header{name, certifiedBy, date, [email, effectiveDate, documentOptionalEmail], staff-payment fields}, business{foundingDate, identifier, legalName, legalType}, <filingType>{...}}`.
- Staff-payment header fields by `staffPaymentData.option`:
  - FAS: `routingSlipNumber`, `priority`.
  - BCOL: `bcolAccountNumber`, `datNumber`, `folioNumber`, `priority`.
  - NO_FEE: `waiveFees`.
  - NONE: nothing.
- Response: `header.filingId`, `header.isPaymentActionRequired`, `header.paymentToken`. An error response may carry `data.filing`, `errors` and `warnings`.

## Decisions
- Views and filings: `AgmExtension`, `AgmLocationChg`, `AmalgamationOut`, `AnnualReport`, `ConsentAmalgamationOut`, `ConsentContinuationOut`, `ContinuationOut`, `StandaloneDirectorsFiling`, `StandaloneOfficeAddressFiling`.
- `AmalgamationSelection.startAmalgamation` creates a draft amalgamation application. Role by type: HORIZONTAL→PRIMARY, VERTICAL→HOLDING, REGULAR→AMALGAMATING. A missing identifier throws "Invalid business identifier".
- `Dashboard` and `EntityMenu` route to the filings. `EntityHeader` and `Signin`/`Signout` are display and auth redirects.
- `saveFiling(isDraft)`: if `filingId===0`, call `LegalServices.hasPendingTasks`. If true, set `saveErrors` ("Another draft filing already exists…") and throw. A failed check sets "Unable to check server for pending tasks." and throws. Then call `updateFiling` if `filingId>0`, else `createFiling`. The catch stores `response.data.errors` and `warnings`, then re-throws.
- `onClickFilePay`:
  - Returns if `busySaving`.
  - Where the view has `isPageValid`, an invalid page sets `showErrors` and returns.
  - Staff (`isRoleStaff && !fromStaffPayment`) get the staff-payment dialog first, in the views that have one.
  - A 402 (`StatusCodes.PAYMENT_REQUIRED`) clears `haveChanges` and sets `paymentErrorDialog`. Any other error sets `saveErrorReason=FILE_PAY`. Both return `error.response.data.filing` or null, and neither is re-raised.
  - With no error, `onClickFilePayFinish` runs. It needs `filingId>0`. It navigates to pay if `isPaymentActionRequired`, else to the dashboard.
- `onClickSave` and `onClickSaveResume` return if `busySaving`. They set `saveErrorReason` SAVE or SAVE_RESUME on error. The Finish functions need `filingId>0` and clear `haveChanges`; resume also calls `goToDashboard(true)`.
- `onSaveErrorDialogRetry` re-runs the action matching `saveErrorReason`. `onSaveErrorDialogOkay` calls the matching Finish function.
- `goToDashboard`: leaves at once if `!haveChanges || force`. Otherwise it opens the confirm dialog. Cancel clears `haveChanges` and leaves.
- `onPaymentErrorDialogExit`: staff stay on the page; others go to the dashboard.
- `fetchDraftFiling` refuses a draft when the filing type, status (must be DRAFT), `business.identifier` vs `getIdentifier`, or `business.legalName` vs `getLegalName` do not match. It restores staff-payment option from `routingSlipNumber`, `bcolAccountNumber` and `waiveFees`. Errors set `resumeErrorDialog`, are logged, and are swallowed.
- `isPayRequired` = `totalFee>0`. It only changes the button text.
- `AgmExtension` and `AgmLocationChg`:
  - A non-zero `filingId` redirects to the dashboard, so drafts are not resumable.
  - `AgmExtension` stops with `notEligibleExtensionDialog` if `!data.isEligible`.
- `AmalgamationOut` and `ContinuationOut`: `created()` throws or opens the resume dialog if `!isRoleStaff`.
- `EntityMenu`:
  - Entities allowed by feature flags `supported-*-entities`.
  - Change-info and dissolve are blocked when `!isGoodStanding && !isRoleStaff`. They emit `notInGoodStanding`, with `NigsMessage.CHANGE_COMPANY_INFO` or `DISSOLVE`.
  - Otherwise they are disabled by `!isAllowed(BUSINESS_INFORMATION)` or `!isAllowed(VOLUNTARY_DISSOLUTION)`.
  - Change-info route: coop → `/special-resolution`, firm → `/change`, else `/alteration`.
- `DigitalCredentials.mounted`: redirects to `Routes.DASHBOARD` if `!isAllowed(DIGITAL_CREDENTIALS)`.
- `Dashboard`: buttons disabled by `isAllowed(ADDRESS_CHANGE or DIRECTOR_CHANGE)`, `isHistorical` and `isDisableNonBenCorps`. A base company opens the COA warning, a firm goes to `/change`, others go to standalone addresses.
- `AnnualReport.mounted`: leaves for the dashboard if identifier, year or filingId is missing, if a coop lacks `arMinDate`/`arMaxDate`, or if a base company lacks `nextARDate`.

## Boundaries
- No view checks permission on its entry points (`isAllowed` only disables buttons). Only the `isRoleStaff` checks above apply.
- Duplicate guard: `busySaving` only, plus `hasPendingTasks` for new filings. No retry on `LegalServices` calls.
- Committed before failure: a draft saved (filingId set) stays saved if a later step fails.

## Hazards
- `AmalgamationOut` and `ContinuationOut` save steps swallow errors: save errors become `saveErrorReason` and the flow continues. In `StandaloneOfficeAddressFiling.onClickSave`, the catch returns the filing but does not set `saveErrorReason`, so `onClickSaveFinish` runs as if the save succeeded.
- `onClickFilePayFinish` builds the pay URL without checking `paymentToken` or `filingId` format. `navigate(payUrl)` has no error handling.
- `EntityMenu` references `isEntityCoop` and `isEntityFirm`, whose definitions are not in the notes.

## Open first
- `src/views/AnnualReport.vue`: the fullest save, resume and pay flow.
- `src/views/StandaloneDirectorsFiling.vue`: edit and review pages, plus fee codes.
- `src/components/EntityInfo/EntityMenu.vue`: permission and feature-flag gating of filing entry.
- `src/views/AmalgamationSelection.vue`: draft business creation.

## Connections
- [L3]/[L4] legal-api `business_filings`: the UI posts the filing there through `saveFiling`. It checks nothing on the payload shape. The API validates the schema (400 on failure). In the v1 and v2 `save_filing` code, a PUT updates an existing filing and a `T…` identifier is a bootstrap business. A 402 error is read by the UI as payment required.
- [L2] business-pay `FilingStatus.DRAFT`: the UI compares `header.status` to DRAFT on resume. The queue service uses that status for payment, so a filing already PAID or PENDING is refused for resume (error dialog).
- [L5], [L6], [L8], [L9], [L11], [L12] dialogs (`PaymentErrorDialog`, `NotEligibleExtensionDialog`, `ResumeErrorDialog`, `SaveErrorDialog`, `TechnicalErrorDialog`, `FetchErrorDialog`): views toggle them by flag and handle their emits (`exit`, `retry`, `okay`). Each hides contact info for staff. `SaveErrorDialog` retry is disabled by `disableRetry`.
- [L7] `TodoList`: views use `$refs.confirm.open`, which resolves on Yes and rejects on Cancel. This is the same dialog API as the unsaved-changes prompt.
- [L10] `BusinessNameForeign`: `AmalgamationOut` and `ContinuationOut` embed it. It emits a normalised name and a `valid` flag.
- [L1] colin-api `business.py`: only the founding date (`getFoundingDate`) is used, in the filing payload and in `allowChange`. It is not a UI contract.

## Role
Front-end filing UI (Vue, `src/views`, `src/components/EntityInfo`, `src/assets`). It collects filing data, saves or files it through `LegalServices` (create, update, fetch, `hasPendingTasks`), then sends the user to the pay UI (`getAuthWebUrl + 'makepayment/' + paymentToken + '/' + encodeURIComponent(baseUrl + '?filing_id=' + filingId)`) or back to the business dashboard. The notes show no credential on these calls. `src/assets` holds SCSS and the BC Sans font (OFL licence); they hold no logic.

## Contract
- In: route query `filing_id` (0 = new, >0 = resume draft, NaN = invalid), store getters (`getIdentifier`, `getLegalName`, `getLegalType`, `isRoleStaff`, `isAllowed(AllowableActions.*)`), feature flags.
- Out, filing payload `{header{name, certifiedBy, date, [email, effectiveDate, documentOptionalEmail], staff-payment fields}, business{foundingDate, identifier, legalName, legalType}, <filingType>{...}}`.
- Staff-payment header fields by `staffPaymentData.option`:
  - FAS: `routingSlipNumber`, `priority`.
  - BCOL: `bcolAccountNumber`, `datNumber`, `folioNumber`, `priority`.
  - NO_FEE: `waiveFees`.
  - NONE: nothing.
- Response: `header.filingId`, `header.isPaymentActionRequired`, `header.paymentToken`. An error response may carry `data.filing`, `errors` and `warnings`.

## Decisions
- Views and filings: `AgmExtension`, `AgmLocationChg`, `AmalgamationOut`, `AnnualReport`, `ConsentAmalgamationOut`, `ConsentContinuationOut`, `ContinuationOut`, `StandaloneDirectorsFiling`, `StandaloneOfficeAddressFiling`.
- `AmalgamationSelection.startAmalgamation` creates a draft amalgamation application. Role by type: HORIZONTAL→PRIMARY, VERTICAL→HOLDING, REGULAR→AMALGAMATING. A missing identifier throws "Invalid business identifier".
- `Dashboard` and `EntityMenu` route to the filings. `EntityHeader` and `Signin`/`Signout` are display and auth redirects.
- `saveFiling(isDraft)`: if `filingId===0`, call `LegalServices.hasPendingTasks`. If true, set `saveErrors` ("Another draft filing already exists…") and throw. A failed check sets "Unable to check server for pending tasks." and throws. Then call `updateFiling` if `filingId>0`, else `createFiling`. The catch stores `response.data.errors` and `warnings`, then re-throws.
- `onClickFilePay`:
  - Returns if `busySaving`.
  - Where the view has `isPageValid`, an invalid page sets `showErrors` and returns.
  - Staff (`isRoleStaff && !fromStaffPayment`) get the staff-payment dialog first, in the views that have one.
  - A 402 (`StatusCodes.PAYMENT_REQUIRED`) clears `haveChanges` and sets `paymentErrorDialog`. Any other error sets `saveErrorReason=FILE_PAY`. Both return `error.response.data.filing` or null, and neither is re-raised.
  - With no error, `onClickFilePayFinish` runs. It needs `filingId>0`. It navigates to pay if `isPaymentActionRequired`, else to the dashboard.
- `onClickSave` and `onClickSaveResume` return if `busySaving`. They set `saveErrorReason` SAVE or SAVE_RESUME on error. The Finish functions need `filingId>0` and clear `haveChanges`; resume also calls `goToDashboard(true)`.
- `onSaveErrorDialogRetry` re-runs the action matching `saveErrorReason`. `onSaveErrorDialogOkay` calls the matching Finish function.
- `goToDashboard`: leaves at once if `!haveChanges || force`. Otherwise it opens the confirm dialog. Cancel clears `haveChanges` and leaves.
- `onPaymentErrorDialogExit`: staff stay on the page; others go to the dashboard.
- `fetchDraftFiling` refuses a draft when the filing type, status (must be DRAFT), `business.identifier` vs `getIdentifier`, or `business.legalName` vs `getLegalName` do not match. It restores staff-payment option from `routingSlipNumber`, `bcolAccountNumber` and `waiveFees`. Errors set `resumeErrorDialog`, are logged, and are swallowed.
- `isPayRequired` = `totalFee>0`. It only changes the button text.
- `AgmExtension` and `AgmLocationChg`:
  - A non-zero `filingId` redirects to the dashboard, so drafts are not resumable.
  - `AgmExtension` stops with `notEligibleExtensionDialog` if `!data.isEligible`.
- `AmalgamationOut` and `ContinuationOut`: `created()` throws or opens the resume dialog if `!isRoleStaff`.
- `EntityMenu`:
  - Entities allowed by feature flags `supported-*-entities`.
  - Change-info and dissolve are blocked when `!isGoodStanding && !isRoleStaff`. They emit `notInGoodStanding`, with `NigsMessage.CHANGE_COMPANY_INFO` or `DISSOLVE`.
  - Otherwise they are disabled by `!isAllowed(BUSINESS_INFORMATION)` or `!isAllowed(VOLUNTARY_DISSOLUTION)`.
  - Change-info route: coop → `/special-resolution`, firm → `/change`, else `/alteration`.
- `DigitalCredentials.mounted`: redirects to `Routes.DASHBOARD` if `!isAllowed(DIGITAL_CREDENTIALS)`.
- `Dashboard`: buttons disabled by `isAllowed(ADDRESS_CHANGE or DIRECTOR_CHANGE)`, `isHistorical` and `isDisableNonBenCorps`. A base company opens the COA warning, a firm goes to `/change`, others go to standalone addresses.
- `AnnualReport.mounted`: leaves for the dashboard if identifier, year or filingId is missing, if a coop lacks `arMinDate`/`arMaxDate`, or if a base company lacks `nextARDate`.

## Boundaries
- No view checks permission on its entry points (`isAllowed` only disables buttons). Only the `isRoleStaff` checks above apply.
- Duplicate guard: `busySaving` only, plus `hasPendingTasks` for new filings. No retry on `LegalServices` calls.
- Committed before failure: a draft saved (filingId set) stays saved if a later step fails.

## Hazards
- `AmalgamationOut` and `ContinuationOut` save steps swallow errors: save errors become `saveErrorReason` and the flow continues. In `StandaloneOfficeAddressFiling.onClickSave`, the catch returns the filing but does not set `saveErrorReason`, so `onClickSaveFinish` runs as if the save succeeded.
- `onClickFilePayFinish` builds the pay URL without checking `paymentToken` or `filingId` format. `navigate(payUrl)` has no error handling.
- `EntityMenu` references `isEntityCoop` and `isEntityFirm`, whose definitions are not in the notes.

## Open first
- `src/views/AnnualReport.vue`: the fullest save, resume and pay flow.
- `src/views/StandaloneDirectorsFiling.vue`: edit and review pages, plus fee codes.
- `src/components/EntityInfo/EntityMenu.vue`: permission and feature-flag gating of filing entry.
- `src/views/AmalgamationSelection.vue`: draft business creation.

## Connections
- [L3]/[L4] legal-api `business_filings`: the UI posts the filing there through `saveFiling`. It checks nothing on the payload shape. The API validates the schema (400 on failure). In the v1 and v2 `save_filing` code, a PUT updates an existing filing and a `T…` identifier is a bootstrap business. A 402 error is read by the UI as payment required.
- [L2] business-pay `FilingStatus.DRAFT`: the UI compares `header.status` to DRAFT on resume. The queue service uses that status for payment, so a filing already PAID or PENDING is refused for resume (error dialog).
- [L5], [L6], [L8], [L9], [L11], [L12] dialogs (`PaymentErrorDialog`, `NotEligibleExtensionDialog`, `ResumeErrorDialog`, `SaveErrorDialog`, `TechnicalErrorDialog`, `FetchErrorDialog`): views toggle them by flag and handle their emits (`exit`, `retry`, `okay`). Each hides contact info for staff. `SaveErrorDialog` retry is disabled by `disableRetry`.
- [L7] `TodoList`: views use `$refs.confirm.open`, which resolves on Yes and rejects on Cancel. This is the same dialog API as the unsaved-changes prompt.
- [L10] `BusinessNameForeign`: `AmalgamationOut` and `ContinuationOut` embed it. It emits a normalised name and a `valid` flag.
- [L1] colin-api `business.py`: only the founding date (`getFoundingDate`) is used, in the filing payload and in `allowChange`. It is not a UI contract.

structured.brief:
## Role
The legal-api v2 business REST layer (Flask, `legal_api/resources/v2/...`): business lookup/search, addresses, aliases, parties, directors, resolutions, comments, documents, tasks, filings (create/update/delete/cancel payment), digital credentials, furnishings, internal COLIN-sync and BN-move endpoints. It also holds `MinioService` (the Minio wrapper) and the `DCConnection` model. It hands work to the payment service, namex, Minio, the digital-credentials service, a queue (`queue.publish_json`) and NATS, and the DB models.

## Contract
- In: HTTP with a JWT. Internal callers: `colin` role (`/internal/filings*`, `/internal/tax_ids`), `system` role (`/internal/filings/future_effective`, `/internal/bnmove`), and the aca-py webhook `POST /topic/<topic_name>`. The entity-filer worker (queue_services) calls `MinioService.get_file`/`put_file`. The digital-credentials worker reads `DCConnection`.
- Out: JSON responses. Queue payload `{'filing': {'id': filing.id}}` for COLIN filings. NATS events `bc.registry.bnmove` (emailer subject) and `bc.registry.business.bn` (entity-event subject).
- Payment service: `POST {PAYMENT_SVC_URL}` (invoice), `GET/DELETE {PAYMENT_SVC_URL}/{payment_token}`, and `POST .../{payment_token}/receipts`. All send `Authorization: Bearer <caller's JWT>`. Invoice payload: `{businessInfo, filingInfo{filingTypes,...}, details, accountInfo?}`, timeout 20s.

## Decisions
- Filing save (`saving_filings`): `T…` identifiers use `RegistrationBootstrap`. `draft` or `only_validate` skips validation, and `only_validate` returns the JSON with 200. A change-requested filing goes to `resubmit_filing_for_review`, which sets the Review to RESUBMITTED and the filing to awaiting review.
- `ListFilingResource.check_authorization`: needs both `authorized(identifier, jwt, ['edit'])` and `is_allowed(...)`.
- `put_basic_checks`: empty body gives 400. `filing_id` with a non-PUT method gives 403. A missing filing type gives 400. A non-new-business type with no business gives 400.
- `complete_filing`: a COLIN-source filing goes to `process_colin_filing`. Otherwise (not draft) it runs `check_and_update_nr`, `set_effective_date` and `get_filing_types`, then `create_invoice`. Invoice responses map as: 200/201 → 201; 400 → 402 with `payment_status_code` set; timeout/connection error → 402.
- `get_filing_types`: builds fee codes per filing type (dissolution, correction, changeOfDirectors "free" variant, etc.).
- `delete_filings`: `authorized(['edit'])`. A locked filing gets a deletion-locked response. DRAFT/PENDING filing deletion is refused with 401 in `ListFilingResource`. Minio files are deleted, then the filing, then the bootstrap (deregister + delete) for `T…`.
- PATCH filing (cancel payment): `authorized(['edit'])`. It calls `DELETE` on the payment service, then `reset_filing_to_draft()` only if the status is 200/202.
- `check_and_update_nr`: for new-business filings with an NR and an effective date, if `namex.is_date_past_expiration`, it calls `update_nr_as_future_effective`.
- `get_ledger_listing`: PDF accept gives 406; an invalid `datetime_str` gives 400.
- Business GET `/<identifier>`: `T…` gives a "No information on temp registrations." message with 200. A missing business gives 404. `account` adds `accountId` only when the caller has SYSTEM_ROLE or ACCOUNT_IDENTITY and the org id matches. Authorization is commented out (#22143).
- Business POST: the filing type must be in `NEW_BUSINESS_FILING_TYPES`, else 400. The sequence is `create_bootstrap`, `register_bootstrap`, then `saving_filings`. A registration failure deletes the bootstrap (exceptions suppressed) and returns 503.
- `POST /search`: needs SYSTEM_ROLE. `identifiers` must be a list, else 400. Draft filings with `business_id` NULL are returned with `nrNumber` and `effectiveDate`.
- Tasks: an `NR…` identifier is checked with `namex.validate_nr`, and a non-consumable NR gives 403. Pay-api connection error gives 503. Annual-report todos are generated per year up to the current year. SP/GP skip them.
- Digital credentials (all `@can_access_digital_credentials`):
  - Invitation: an active connection gives 422. An existing `invitation`-state connection is reused. Otherwise a new one is created and saved.

## Decisions
- Filing save (`saving_filings`): `T…` identifiers use `RegistrationBootstrap`. `draft` or `only_validate` skips validation, and `only_validate` returns the JSON with 200. A change-requested filing goes to `resubmit_filing_for_review`, which sets the Review to RESUBMITTED and the filing to awaiting review.
- `ListFilingResource.check_authorization`: needs both `authorized(identifier, jwt, ['edit'])` and `is_allowed(...)`.
- `put_basic_checks`: empty body gives 400. `filing_id` with a non-PUT method gives 403. A missing filing type gives 400. A non-new-business type with no business gives 400.
- `complete_filing`: a COLIN-source filing goes to `process_colin_filing`. Otherwise (not draft) it runs `check_and_update_nr`, `set_effective_date` and `get_filing_types`, then `create_invoice`. Base class for parsing and validating TDI17 fixed-width EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer) records. Stores record_type (1=header, 2=detail, 7=trailer), content string, index, and errors array. Methods: is_valid_length(length=EFTConstants.EXPECTED_LINE_LENGTH.value) returns true if content length matches, else false; validate_record_type(expected_record_type) compares self.record_type and adds EFTParseError(INVALID_RECORD_TYPE, index) if mismatch; extract_value(start_index, end_index) slices and strips content; parse_decimal(value, error) parses sign-trailing-minus format, returns Decimal or None with error added; parse_int(value, error), parse_date(date_str, error, format=DATE_FORMAT), parse_datetime(datetime_str, error, format=DATE_TIME_FORMAT) similarly return parsed value or None + error; add_error(error) appends to errors and sets index; has_errors() returns len > 0; get_error_messages() returns list of error.message strings. TDI17 spec in comments details header (creation date/time YYYYMMDD/HHMM, deposit date range), detail records (ministry/program codes, deposit date, location, transaction description 40-char, amounts in cents right-justified zero-padded, currency/exchange/CAD amount, bank/batch/JV fields), trailer (detail count, total CAD). ## entity-emailer (lear/queue_services/entity-emailer)

NATS Streaming worker that takes email-event messages published by other entity services (filer, bn, etc.), tracks each in a MessageProcessing record, builds the email with a type-specific processor, and POSTs it to the notify API. After a successful dissolution send it updates the Furnishing record.

**Contract**
- In: NATS message to `cb_subscription_handler(msg)` (`worker.py`), one at a time. Either a cloud event (`type` like `bc.registry.names.request`, `bc.registry.affiliation`, `bc.registry.bnmove`, `bc.registry.dissolution`) or a legacy `{'email': {'type', 'option', 'filingId', ...}}`. The notes show no auth check on the handler.
- Out: `send_email(email, token)` does `requests.post` to `APP_CONFIG.NOTIFY_API_URL` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (from `AccountService.get_bearer_token()`) and JSON body `{recipients, content:{body,...}, requestBy?}`. Anything other than 200 raises `EmailException`.
- Also `publish_event(payload)` publishes to `ENTITY_EVENT_PUBLISH_OPTIONS['subject']` via `qsm.service.publish`. Failures are logged and swallowed.
- Writes MessageProcessing rows through `MessageProcessingService`. Writes Furnishing status via `involuntary_dissolution_stage_1_notification.post_process`.

**Decisions**
- `process_email` routes on `etype`/`option`:
  - `names.request` with option in BEFORE_EXPIRY/EXPIRED/RENEWAL/UPGRADE/REFUND goes to `nr_notification`; otherwise it goes to `name_request`.
  - `affiliation`, `bnmove` and `businessNumber` go to `affiliation_notification`, `bn_notification.process_bn_move` and `bn_notification.process`.
  - `dissolution` with a furnishing name in `PROCESSABLE_FURNISHING_NAMES` goes to the stage-1 processor; otherwise it is skipped and logged.
  - amalgamationApplication, continuationIn and incorporationApplication with option `mras` go to `mras_notification`.
  - annualReport with option `reminder` goes to `ar_reminder_notification`, with `flags.is_on('disable-specific-service-provider')`.
  - agmLocationChange and agmExtension go to their processors only when option == COMPLETED.
  - Each of dissolution, registration, restoration, changeOfRegistration, correction, consentContinuationOut, continuationOut, specialResolution, amalgamationApplication and continuationIn has its own processor.
  - Any other type in `filing_notification.FILING_TYPE_CONVERTER`, except annualReport COMPLETED, goes to `filing_notification`. It sends only if the email is truthy.
- `tracker.get_message_context_properties` builds the dedupe key:
  - Cloud-event types use `source` plus `email_msg['id']`.
  - Legacy types use `{etype}_{option}_{filingId}`, or `{etype}_{identifier}` (businessNumber), `{etype}_{new_bn}` (bnmove), `{etype}_{filing_id}` (affiliation) and `{etype}_{option}_{ar_year}_{business_id}` (AR reminder). Per-type conditions are in the function.
- `is_processable_message`:
  - It returns (False, None) if the message_id is missing, or if source is missing for a cloud event.
  - It looks the record up by source and id, or by id alone.
  - It returns (False, msg) if `message_seen_count > MSG_RETRY_NUM`.
  - It returns (True, msg) if msg is None or its status is FAILED. The notes do not say what it returns for PROCESSING or COMPLETED records.
- `start_tracking_message` calls `update_message_status_to_processing` if a tracker exists, else `create_processing_message`.
- `mark_tracking_message_as_failed` truncates the error to 1000 characters. It updates by status: PROCESSING → `update_message_status_to_failed`, FAILED → `update_failed_message`, no tracker → `create_failed_message`.
- `send_email` raises `QueueException` if the email, recipients, content or body is missing or empty.
- Dissolution: after a successful send, `post_process(PROCESSED)`. On exception, `post_process(FAILED)` and re-raise.

**Error boundaries**
- `OperationalError` and `EmailException`: the tracker is marked failed and the exception is re-raised, so the message stays on the queue for redelivery.
- `QueueException` and any other `Exception`: the tracker is marked failed and the exception is not re-raised, so the message is dropped.
- Tracker creation happens before processing. The notes show no error handling around tracker or service calls.
- `process_email` needs a Flask app, else it raises `QueueException`.

**Hazards**
- Dedupe depends on message_id construction. If no rule matches, there is no id, so the message is not processable. The notes do not show what happens to it next.
- Only `EmailException` and `OperationalError` are retried. Everything else is dropped after being marked FAILED.
- A failed PDF fetch in the stage-1 processor returns no attachment, so the email goes out without it and is not retried (L6).

**Open first**
- `src/entity_emailer/worker.py`: handler, routing, `send_email`, error policy.
- `message_tracker/tracker.py`: message_id rules, processability check, status transitions.
- `email_processors/involuntary_dissolution_stage_1_notification.py` (L6): `PROCESSABLE_FURNISHING_NAMES`, `post_process`.
- `tracker/services/message_processing_service.py` (L5): persistence.

**Connections**
- L5: tracker calls `find_message_by_message_id`, `find_message_by_source_and_message_id`, `create_message` and the update methods. Saves are unconditional, with no retry.
- L6: the dissolution gate reads `PROCESSABLE_FURNISHING_NAMES`. `post_process` sets Furnishing status and notes 'Failure to send email' on FAILED.
- L7: `EmailException` and `QueueException` come from the shared exceptions module and drive the requeue-or-drop policy.
- L4: `flags.is_on` is read for the AR reminder. It returns False on any error, so a flag outage silently reads as off.
- L2, L3: `NOTIFY_API_URL` is defined in auth-api config and in the payment-jobs vault env. This part posts there with the bearer token and checks only for 200.
- L9: entity-bn publishes the email event (type `businessNumber`) consumed here. Its email-publish exception is re-raised on its side.
- L8: entity-filer's `publish_event` produces the filing events routed here. Its notes show failures only logged.
- L1: account-mailer is a separate service. It shares only the "send to notification system" role and uses a different path.
- L10, L11, L12: entity-filer processors. They share only `QueueException` and do not cross this part's boundary.

Queue worker processes Pub/Sub messages and sends emails. Entry point: POST `/` with `@ensure_authorized_queue_user` authorization check. Extracts CloudEvent, returns 200 immediately if missing. Checks PubSubMessageProcessing.find_by_cloud_event_id_and_type(event_message.id, event_message.type); if found, skips processing. Records processing by creating PubSubMessageProcessing with cloud_event_id, message_type, processed timestamp; commits to db before routing. Routes via 16 message-type handlers (handle_drawdown_request, handle_pad_account_create, etc.). Each handler checks message_type enum and calls email processors, passes tokens where needed. Catches all exceptions, logs error, returns 200 OK regardless.

Configuration file providing Flask application settings across dev/test/prod environments via environment variables. Entry point: get_named_config(config_name='production') checks if name in ['production','staging','default']→ProdConfig(), 'testing'→TestConfig(), 'development'→DevConfig(), else raises KeyError; no validation of name before instantiation. _Config base class defines constants: SECRET_KEY='a secret', TESTING=False, DEBUG=False, ALEMBIC_INI='migrations/alembic.ini', SKIPPED_MIGRATIONS=['authorizations_view']. PostgreSQL: SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI from DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME, DB_HOST, DB_PORT via either DB_UNIX_SOCKET (psycopg2://) or TCP format. structured.brief:
## entity-filer (queue_services/entity-filer)

NATS queue worker that takes filing messages from a NATS Streaming subscription and applies each filing to the Business Database (business, filing, entity state). It hands work to per-type filing processors, the account/affiliation/name-request services, Minio (certified PDFs), and publishes email and event messages (NATS and GCP).

### Contract
- In: NATS message callback `cb_subscription_handler` decodes the message into `filing_msg` (shape: `filing_msg['filing']['id']` is the filing id, though the lookup line is commented out in one excerpt). It passes `filing_msg` and `FLASK_APP` to `process_filing`.
- Out:
  - Writes business, filing and transaction records (`filing_submission._meta_data` = JSON of `filing_meta.asjson`, camelCase keys, dates via `json_serial`).
  - `publish_email_message(qsm, APP_CONFIG.EMAIL_PUBLISH_OPTIONS['subject'], filing_submission, status)` to the emailer NATS subject.
  - `publish_event` to `APP_CONFIG.ENTITY_EVENT_PUBLISH_OPTIONS['subject']` on NATS.
  - `publish_gcp_queue_event` to `gcp_queue.publish(BUSINESS_EVENTS_TOPIC, to_queue_message(ce))`.
  - `publish_mras_email` sends the emailer message with type 'mras'.
  - `replace_file_with_certified_copy` puts the stamped PDF to Minio.

### Decisions
- `cb_subscription_handler` error handling:
  - `OperationalError` and `FilingException` are logged and re-raised, so the framework can redeliver.
  - `QueueException` and any other `Exception` go to Sentry `capture_message('Queue Error:'+json)`, are logged and are swallowed. The message is dropped.
- `process_filing`: a missing `flask_app` raises `QueueException('Flask App not available.')`.
- `process_filing`: if `filing_core_submission.status == Filing.Status.COMPLETED`, it logs a warning and returns None, None. This is the only idempotence check.
- `process_filing`: if `filing_type == CORRECTION`, it sets `is_correction`, and `filing_meta.correction = {}`.
- Dispatch: each key present in the filing JSON (`filing.get('alteration')`, `annualReport`, `incorporationApplication`, `amalgamationApplication`, `continuationIn`, `specialResolution`, etc., 25 types) calls its module's `process()`.
  - Annual report, change of address and dissolution also read the `enable-involuntary-dissolution` flag.
  - `changeOfDirectors` gets `colinIds` from `filing_submission.colin_event_ids`.
- Commit order:
  1. Set `transaction_id`, `set_processed(business_type)` and `_meta_data`, then add and commit.
  2. For AMALGAMATIONAPPLICATION, CONTINUATIONIN, CONVERSION, INCORPORATIONAPPLICATION, REGISTRATION: set `business_id` and commit. Then update affiliation (not for CONVERSION), consume the name request, update the business profile, and publish the MRAS email.
  3. Otherwise, per type in `legal_filings`:
     - `update_entity` runs for ALTERATION, CHANGEOFREGISTRATION, CORRECTION, DISSOLUTION, PUTBACKON, RESTORATION.
     - `consume_nr` and `update_business_profile` run for ALTERATION, CHANGEOFREGISTRATION, CHANGEOFNAME, CORRECTION, RESTORATION. The profile update is skipped for CHANGEOFNAME.
  4. Publish the email, then the event.
- `publish_mras_email` sends only for AMALGAMATIONAPPLICATION, CONTINUATIONIN and INCORPORATIONAPPLICATION.
- `get_run_version` appends `OPENSHIFT_BUILD_COMMIT` to `__version__` (2.128.0) when it is set.

### Boundaries
- No permission check on any entry point: `cb_subscription_handler`, `process_filing`, the publish functions.
- The email, NATS event and GCP event publishes are each wrapped in try/except. They report to Sentry (the event publish also prints) and swallow the error. There is no retry and no duplicate-publish guard.
- Commits happen before affiliation, name request, profile and publish steps. A failure there is not rolled back.
- `replace_file_with_certified_copy`:
  1. Builds the registrar stamp via `PdfService().create_registrars_stamp(RegistrarStampData)`.
  2. Stamps the first page via `stamp_pdf(..., only_first_page=True)`.
  3. Calls `MinioService.put_file(key, bytes, size)`.
  
  It has no error handling or input validation. The notes show no credentials passed by the caller.
- `get_named_config`: production, staging and default give `ProdConfig`; testing gives `TestConfig`; development gives `DevConfig`; anything else raises `KeyError`. Config does not check that required environment variables are set.

### Hazards
1. A swallowed `QueueException` or generic exception removes the message from the queue. A bad filing is lost, with only a Sentry message.
2. A failure after the first commit leaves the filing marked processed but with no affiliation, name-request consumption or events. A redelivery then returns early because the status is COMPLETED, so nothing completes the missing steps.
3. `json_serial` raises `TypeError` for anything other than date or datetime.

### Open first
- `worker.py`: `cb_subscription_handler`, `process_filing`, the publish helpers.
- `filing_meta.py`: metadata serialization.
- `utils.py`: certified-copy stamping.
- `config.py`: NATS subjects, topics and service URLs.

### Connections
- [L1] legal-api `minio.py`: `MinioService.put_file(key, data, length)` calls Minio `put_object(bucket, key, data, length)` with `MINIO_ACCESS_KEY` and `MINIO_ACCESS_SECRET`. No permission or error handling on either side, so an upload failure propagates up unchecked from `replace_file_with_certified_copy`.
- [L7] legal-api `pdf_service.py`: `PdfService.create_registrars_stamp(RegistrarStampData)` and `stamp_pdf(BytesIO, stamp, only_first_page=True)`. It stamps only page 0. The stamp reads "Filed on <date>", "(Corrected)" if `is_correction`, the file name and the incorporation number.
- [L5] data-tool `filing_meta.py`: a copy of the same `json_serial` and `FilingMeta`. No cross-part check.
- [L9], [L10] data-tool custom filer: these have their own `process_filing` with a different signature (`config, filing_id, ...`). They do not call this worker's function, so the description of them as callers does not hold here.

structured.brief:
## Role
Entity-filer filing processors (`queue_services/entity-filer/.../filing_processors/`): one module per filing type. Each takes a decoded filing JSON plus ORM objects (`Business`, `Filing` record, `FilingMeta`) from the queue consumer and mutates the legal-DB models and `filing_meta`. Shared helpers live in `filing_components/` and call out to COLIN API, Account service, Namex and Minio.

## Contract
- In: `process(business, filing, filing_rec, filing_meta[, flag_on])`. The signature varies by module, e.g. `correction.process(correction_filing, filing, filing_meta, business)`. The notes show no auth check on any entry point.
- Out: mutated models, `filing_meta.<type>` dicts (from/to names, nrNumber, etc.) and `filing_rec._filing_json`. Most modules do not commit; the notes show no save in them (`correction.py` calls `original_filing.save_to_session()`). `QueueException` is the failure signal to the caller.

## Decisions
- Creation filings (`incorporation_filing`, `registration`, `amalgamation_application`, `continuation_in`, `conversion` for corps): `business` not None -> `QueueException`; filing section missing -> `QueueException`; corp number or `update_business_info` falsy -> `QueueException`. `filing_rec.colin_event_ids` truthy -> corp_num taken from the filing; else `business_info.get_next_corp_num`. Business state is set ACTIVE.
- `conversion.process`: `business.legal_type` in SP/GP -> `_process_firms_conversion`, else `_process_corps_conversion`.
- `correction.process`: `correctedFilingType != 'conversion'` -> `correct_business_data`; conversion -> `_status=PENDING_CORRECTION` and `skip_status_listener=True`.
- `dissolution.process`: voluntary dissolution of SP/GP takes `dissolutionDate` from the filing, otherwise `effective_date`. Administrative dissolution deletes amalgamation records. COOP goes to `_update_cooperative`, which returns early for administrative. `flag_on` -> `BatchProcessing` QUEUED->COMPLETED. State -> HISTORICAL.
- `put_back_on` and `restoration`: state ACTIVE, `dissolution_date=None`. Restoration sets `restoration_expiry_date` only for limited types, otherwise None.
- `continuation_out`: state HISTORICAL, jurisdiction set.
- `annual_report`: `flag_on` and `in_dissolution` and `InvoluntaryDissolutionService.check_business_eligibility` returns False -> batch status WITHDRAWN. `requires_agm` gates the AGM date.
- `change_of_address`: `flag_on`, in dissolution, batch status not COMPLETED/WITHDRAWN, and `utcnow+60d > trigger_date` -> `trigger_date = utcnow+62d`, `changeOfAddressDelay` set.
- `change_of_directors`: director matched by case-insensitive name; actions are appointed/ceased/modified. If `colinIds` is present, directors not in the filing are ceased. An unresolvable name -> `QueueException`.
- `amalgamation_application`: horizontal/vertical copies the primary/holding business's data. Amalgamating businesses with a `foreignJurisdiction` are recorded as foreign. Local ones are dissolved (HISTORICAL).
- `filing_components.business_info.get_next_corp_num` returns None unless HTTP 200 and `corpNum <= 9999999`.
- `filing_components.name_request.consume_nr` branches on flag `namex-nro-decommissioned` for the payload shape.

## Boundaries
- `get_next_corp_num`: POST `COLIN_API/{type}` with `Bearer` token from `AccountService.get_bearer_token()`. `ConnectionError` is logged and returns None; no retry. The notes say the endpoint has a TODO to fix.
- `consume_nr`: PATCH `NAMEX_API+nr_num` with Bearer token and JSON `{'state':'CONSUMED','corpNum'}` or `{'consume':{'corpNum'}}`. Non-200 raises `QueueException`, but the surrounding `except Exception` sends it to Sentry and swallows it. It then deletes the bootstrap affiliation.
- `business_profile`: POST (or PUT on 400 `DATA_ALREADY_EXISTS`) to `ACCOUNT_SVC_ENTITY_URL/{identifier}/contacts` with Bearer token. Errors go to Sentry only. `update_affiliation` swallows exceptions, and on failed `create_affiliation` calls `delete_affiliation`.
- `rules_and_memorandum`, `dissolution` and `incorporation_filing` fetch files from `MinioService.get_file` and replace them with a certified copy. There is no error handling or retry.
- `offices.update_offices`: a bare except on delete returns the error list and skips creation. A KeyError on create is recorded and the loop continues.
- `parties.update_parties`: delete failure or KeyError returns an error list, which callers mostly ignore.
- `shares.update_share_structure`: delete failure returns early; bad resolution dates and KeyErrors are recorded and execution continues.
- Many modules wrap extraction in `suppress(IndexError, KeyError, TypeError)`: alteration, change_of_registration, conversion firms, correction, court-order paths. Later steps still run.

## Hazards
1. Failures in the helpers (`update_offices`, `update_parties`, `update_share_structure`) come back as returned error lists. Callers (incorporation, registration, transition, etc.) do not check them in the notes, so a filing can complete with offices, parties or shares missing.
2. Blanket `suppress` and `except` blocks in alteration, correction, change_of_registration and `consume_nr` hide missing data. They also leave partial updates, with no rollback, in a failing run.
3. There is no duplicate guard on corp number reservation, party/role creation, or batch-processing updates, and no retry on COLIN, Minio or Account calls. Reprocessing can duplicate or skip work.

## Open first
- `filing_components/business_info.py`: corp-number reservation, legal name/NAICS, passcode.
- `filing_components/business_profile.py` and `name_request.py`: outbound Account/Namex calls.
- `dissolution.py` and `annual_report.py`: state transitions and batch processing.
- `incorporation_filing.py`: the canonical creation flow.

## Connections
- [L12] `legal_api/services/filings/validations/dissolution.py`: `DissolutionTypes` (VOLUNTARY/ADMINISTRATIVE) is read by `dissolution.py`. The notes show no validation in the filer, so it relies on legal-api validation.
- [L3] `InvoluntaryDissolutionService.check_business_eligibility` and `get_in_dissolution_batch_processing` (legal-api): called by `annual_report`. The service itself shows no permission check or retry.
- [L11] `Document.DIRECTOR_AFFIDAVIT`: used by `continuation_in` for the affidavit document type.
- [L1] `JSON_ROLE_CONVERTER`: only a role-name mapping used by `create_role`. The notes do not show how `filing_components/__init__.py` here connects to the copy in L1.
- L2/L4/L5-L10 (custom filer in data-tool): parallel copies of `update_offices`, `correct_business_data` and `update_aliases`. The notes show no calls into this part, so there is no connection beyond shared names.

## pay-api core package (`pay_api` factory, config, utils, errors)

Flask application factory and shared foundation for the Payment API: config loading, JWT/cache/flags setup, error types, enums, and helper utilities. It calls `CodeService` (DB-backed codes), Alembic, Sentry and LaunchDarkly. Business endpoints and services live elsewhere. `dtos/`, `factory/`, `schemas/` and `utils/__init__.py` hold no code.

## Contract
- Receives: environment variables (config), JWT bearer tokens and an `Account-Id` header (via `UserContext`), and `.env` values.
- Every response carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, registries-trace-id, Account-Id`, and `API: pay_api/{version}`.
- Errors go out as problem JSON `{type, detail?, invalidParams?}` built by `convert_to_response` and `error_to_response`.
- Publishes a Pub/Sub topic name per product via `get_topic_for_corp_type`. The topics come from config: `NAMEX_PAY_TOPIC`, `BUSINESS_PAY_TOPIC`, `STRR_PAY_TOPIC`.
- `Serializable.from_dict` converts camelCase keys to snake_case. `to_dict` converts snake_case to camelCase.

## Decisions
- `create_app`: if `run_mode != 'testing'` and `CLOUD_PLATFORM != 'OCP'`, it runs Alembic `upgrade()` at startup (`execute_migrations`).
- `create_app`: Sentry is initialized only if `SENTRY_ENABLE` lowercased is `'true'` and `SENTRY_DSN` is set.
- `build_cache`: if not `TESTING`, it calls `CodeService.build_all_codes_cache()`.
- `get_named_config`: production, staging and default map to `ProdConfig`; testing to `TestConfig`; development to `DevConfig`; migration to `MigrationConfig`; anything else raises `KeyError`.
- `Flags.init_app`: if `app.env == 'testing'`, it uses the local `flags.json`. Otherwise it initializes LaunchDarkly only if `sdk_key` is set or `app.env != 'production'`.
- `Flags.is_on` and `Flags.value`: they return `default` when there is no client.
- `BusinessException.as_problem_json`: it looks up the DB error config with `CodeService.find_code_value_by_type_and_code(Code.ERROR.value, code)`. If nothing is found, it returns `{'type': code}` plus `detail`.
- `get_bcol_error`: maps BCOL codes 7, 20, 21, 48, 61 and 5 to specific `Error` members. Any other code maps to `BCOL_ERROR`.
- `is_valid_redirect_url`: returns True if `DISABLE_VALID_REDIRECT_URLS` is set. Otherwise the URL must equal an entry in `VALID_REDIRECT_URLS`, or start with the entry's prefix when the entry ends in `*`.
- `get_topic_for_corp_type`: `NRO` goes to the NameX topic. Otherwise it looks up the corp type's `product` via `CodeService`. `BUSINESS` and `BUSINESS_SEARCH` go to the business topic, `STRR` to the STRR topic, and anything else returns None.
- `get_fiscal_year`: month > 3 gives year + 1.
- `is_holiday`: BC holidays (government, optional, public, plus Easter Monday) or a weekend. `get_nearest_business_day` recurses forward past holidays.
- `get_first_and_last_of_frequency`: MONTHLY and WEEKLY give date ranges. Any other frequency gives `(None, None)`.
- `UserContext`: `is_staff`, `is_system` and `is_sandbox` test the token's `realm_access.roles` for the `staff`, `system` and `sandbox` roles. `can_view_bank_info` and `can_view_bank_account_number` check the permission string for `admin`, `view`, `manage_bank_info` and `view_bank_account_number`.
- `string_to_bool`: raises `ValueError` unless the value is 'true' or 'false' (case-insensitive).
- The invoice, payment, routing-slip, EFT and disbursement state machines are defined only as enums in `utils/enums.py`. Transitions live elsewhere.

## Boundaries
- No entry point here has an authorization check. `setup_jwt_manager` sets `JWT_ROLE_CALLBACK` to read `realm_access.roles`. `UserContext` only extracts claims. The notes show no token-expiry or account-ownership check.
- Startup order: db, queue and flags init, then migrations, then ma and endpoints, then Sentry, then cache clear and build.
- `execute_migrations` logs and re-raises, so a failed migration halts startup. The `*.init_app` calls have no try/except.
- `build_cache` swallows and logs any failure, so the app starts with an empty code cache.
- LaunchDarkly: `_get_client` retries `init_app` once on `KeyError`, then logs a warning and returns None. There is no timeout or retry on `variation()`.
- Outbound: Alembic, Sentry (DSN from config), LaunchDarkly (`sdk_key`), and `CodeService`. Config also holds credentials for CFS, PayBC, BCOL, Keycloak and GCP, but no calls using them appear here.

## Hazards
- `_Config` hardcodes `SECRET_KEY = 'a secret'`. Only `ProdConfig` replaces it, using the env var or a random value generated per process.
- `_get_config` does not check for missing env vars. Missing values become None.
- `ServiceUnavailableException.response()` ignores the stored `self.error`.

## Open first
- `__init__.py`: app factory, migrations, cache, JWT roles.
- `config.py`: all env-driven settings and the config classes.
- `utils/util.py`: topic routing, redirect validation, fiscal-year and holiday logic.
- `utils/user_context.py`: role and permission helpers. `exceptions/__init__.py` and `utils/errors.py` hold the error shapes.

## Connections
- [L1] `cgi_ap.py` and [L2] `cgi_ejv.py` (payment-jobs): they call `get_fiscal_year` with the current UTC datetime for CGI batch headers and trailers. [L2] also calls `get_nearest_business_day`. The function applies no timezone conversion in the notes, so the fiscal year follows the datetime passed in.
- [L3] `statement_task.py`: uses the date helpers (`get_week_start_and_end_date`, `get_previous_month_and_year`, `get_local_time`). [L10] `statement_due_task.py` uses `current_local_time`. Both rely on `LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE`.
- [L5] `cfs_bank_name_updater.py` reads `DEFAULT_COUNTRY` and `DEFAULT_CURRENCY`. [L6]/[L7] `cfs_create_account_task.py` read `CFS_RCPT_EFT_WIRE` and `RECEIPT_METHOD_PAD_DAILY` from `utils/constants.py`.
- [L8] reads `PaymentDetailsGlStatus`, [L9] reads `ReverseOperation`, and [L11] reads `EjvFileType`. All are enums from `utils/enums.py`. [L11] relies on `EjvFileType.REFUND` and `NON_GOV_DISBURSEMENT`.
- [L12] uses `generate_transaction_number` from the utils.

- LaunchDarkly: `_get_client` retries `init_app` once on `KeyError`, then logs a warning and returns None. There is no timeout or retry on `variation()`.
- Outbound: Alembic, Sentry (DSN from config), LaunchDarkly (`sdk_key`), and `CodeService`. Config also holds credentials for CFS, PayBC, BCOL, Keycloak and GCP, but no calls using them appear here.

## Hazards
- `_Config` hardcodes `SECRET_KEY = 'a secret'`. Only `ProdConfig` replaces it, using the env var or a random value generated per process.
- `_get_config` does not check for missing env vars. Missing values become None.
- `ServiceUnavailableException.response()` ignores the stored `self.error`.

## Open first
- `__init__.py`: app factory, migrations, cache, JWT roles.
- `config.py`: all env-driven settings and the config classes.
- `utils/util.py`: topic routing, redirect validation, fiscal-year and holiday logic.
- `utils/user_context.py`: role and permission helpers. `exceptions/__init__.py` and `utils/errors.py` hold the error shapes.

## Connections
- [L1] `cgi_ap.py` and [L2] `cgi_ejv.py` (payment-jobs): they call `get_fiscal_year` with the current UTC datetime for CGI batch headers and trailers. [L2] also calls `get_nearest_business_day`. The function applies no timezone conversion in the notes, so the fiscal year follows the datetime passed in.
- [L3] `statement_task.py`: uses the date helpers (`get_week_start_and_end_date`, `get_previous_month_and_year`, `get_local_time`). [L10] `statement_due_task.py` uses `current_local_time`. Both rely on `LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE`.
- [L5] `cfs_bank_name_updater.py` reads `DEFAULT_COUNTRY` and `DEFAULT_CURRENCY`. [L6]/[L7] `cfs_create_account_task.py` read `CFS_RCPT_EFT_WIRE` and `RECEIPT_METHOD_PAD_DAILY` from `utils/constants.py`.
- [L8] reads `PaymentDetailsGlStatus`, [L9] reads `ReverseOperation`, and [L11] reads `EjvFileType`. All are enums from `utils/enums.py`. [L11] relies on `EjvFileType.REFUND` and `NON_GOV_DISBURSEMENT`.
- [L12] uses `generate_transaction_number` from the utils.

structured.brief:
## Role
The pay-api HTTP resource layer (`pay_api/resources`): Flask blueprints under `/api/v1` that validate requests, run role checks, and delegate to the service layer (`PaymentAccountService`, `PaymentService`, `InvoiceService`, `RefundService`, `StatementService`, `EFTShortnameService`, `RoutingSlipService`, `FeeSchedule`, `CFSService` and others). It holds no business logic of its own.

## Contract
- In: HTTP/JSON requests with a JWT. Bodies are checked with `schema_utils.validate(json, schema_name)`, which returns `(valid_format, errors)`.
- Out: JSON, or PDF/CSV for reports and receipts, and `exception.response()` for service errors.
- Invalid bodies return `error_to_response(Error.INVALID_REQUEST, invalid_params=schema_utils.serialize(errors))`.
- `resources/endpoints.py` `Endpoints.init_app` calls `v1_endpoint.init_app(app)`. `v1/__init__.py` `init_app` raises a bare Exception if app is falsy, then registers 21 blueprints (account, account_notifications, account_settings, account_statements, bank_accounts, code, distributions, eft_short_names, fas_refund, fas_routing_slip, fee, fee_schedule, invoice, invoices, invoice_receipt, meta, non_sufficient_funds, ops, payment, refund, transaction). The url prefix comes from `EndpointEnum.API_V1`.

## Decisions
- Account-scoped routes call `check_auth(business_identifier=None, account_id=..., contains_role / one_of_roles=...)`. Its internal condition is not in the notes. Roles used:
  - Statements, notifications and settings: `EDIT_ROLE`. POST on notifications and settings uses `CHANGE_STATEMENT_SETTINGS`. Notifications and settings also pass `is_premium=True`.
  - NSF: one of MAKE_PAYMENT, EDIT_ROLE, VIEW_ROLE.
  - `GET /accounts/<id>/payments`: one of MAKE_PAYMENT, EDIT_ROLE, VIEW_ROLE. `POST` needs MAKE_PAYMENT.
- `post_account_payment`: if the JWT roles include both STAFF and CREATE_CREDITS and `paymentMethod` is EFT or DRAWDOWN, it calls `create_payment_receipt`. Otherwise it calls `create_account_payment`. `retryFailedPayment=true` sets the retry flag. `payOutstandingBalance` and `allInvoiceStatuses` are read only when feature flag `enable-eft-payment-method` is on, else False.
- `post_account` / `put_account`: return 202 if `cfs_account_id` is set and `cfs_account_status == PENDING`. Otherwise POST returns 201 and PUT returns 200. POST also needs `CREATE_SANDBOX_ACCOUNT` for sandbox requests.
- Fees (`fee.py`): `waiveFees` is honoured only if the JWT has STAFF. Otherwise `waive_fees=False`.
- EFT short names: the service lookup returns 404 when it finds nothing. `patch_eft_shortname_link` returns 404 if `link['short_name_id'] != short_name_id`. Refunds: `GET` and `POST /shortname-refund` need EFT_REFUND or EFT_REFUND_APPROVER. `PATCH` needs requires_auth and EFT_REFUND_APPROVER.
- FAS routing slips: a distinct role per route (FAS_CREATE, FAS_SEARCH, FAS_REPORTS, FAS_VIEW, FAS_EDIT, FAS_LINK). Search with no `page` in the body sets `return_all=True`. Comments accept either the `comment` schema or `comment_bcrs_schema`. FAS refund needs FAS_REFUND or FAS_REFUND_APPROVER and returns 202.
- Purchase history: `viewAll=true` needs `VIEW_ALL_TRANSACTIONS` and searches all accounts. Otherwise it needs `EDITOR` and searches that account. The report is a PDF if `Accept` is PDF, else CSV.
- `refund.py`: needs SYSTEM, CREATE_CREDITS or FAS_REFUND. An empty body is accepted.
- Distribution codes: all routes need `MANAGE_GL_CODES`. EFT short names need SYSTEM or MANAGE_EFT.

## Boundaries
- No auth at all (notes show none): `GET /codes/*`, `/fees/schedules`, `/meta/info`, `/ops/healthz` and `/ops/readyz`. `/ops/*` run `select 1` and return 500 on `SQLAlchemyError`.
- `post_transaction`, `patch_transaction` and `POST /payments/<id>/transactions` have no auth check in the notes.
- `patch_account`, `put_account` and `delete_account` show a SYSTEM role but no `@_jwt.requires_auth` in the notes.

## Role
The pay-api HTTP resource layer (`pay_api/resources`): Flask blueprints under `/api/v1` that validate requests, run role checks, and delegate to the service layer (`PaymentAccountService`, `PaymentService`, `InvoiceService`, `RefundService`, `StatementService`, `EFTShortnameService`, `RoutingSlipService`, `FeeSchedule`, `CFSService` and others). It holds no business logic of its own.

## Contract
- In: HTTP/JSON requests with a JWT. Bodies are checked with `schema_utils.validate(json, schema_name)`, which returns `(valid_format, errors)`.
- Out: JSON, or PDF/CSV for reports and receipts, and `exception.response()` for service errors.
- Invalid bodies return `error_to_response(Error.INVALID_REQUEST, invalid_params=schema_utils.serialize(errors))`.
- `resources/endpoints.py` `Endpoints.init_app` calls `v1_endpoint.init_app(app)`. `v1/__init__.py` `init_app` raises a bare Exception if app is falsy, then registers 21 blueprints (account, account_notifications, account_settings, account_statements, bank_accounts, code, distributions, eft_short_names, fas_refund, fas_routing_slip, fee, fee_schedule, invoice, invoices, invoice_receipt, meta, non_sufficient_funds, ops, payment, refund, transaction). The url prefix comes from `EndpointEnum.API_V1`.

## Decisions
- Account-scoped routes call `check_auth(business_identifier=None, account_id=..., contains_role / one_of_roles=...)`. Its internal condition is not in the notes. Roles used:
  - Statements, notifications and settings: `EDIT_ROLE`. POST on notifications and settings uses `CHANGE_STATEMENT_SETTINGS`. Notifications and settings also pass `is_premium=True`.
  - NSF: one of MAKE_PAYMENT, EDIT_ROLE, VIEW_ROLE.
  - `GET /accounts/<id>/payments`: one of MAKE_PAYMENT, EDIT_ROLE, VIEW_ROLE. `POST` needs MAKE_PAYMENT.
- `post_account_payment`: if the JWT roles include both STAFF and CREATE_CREDITS and `paymentMethod` is EFT or DRAWDOWN, it calls `create_payment_receipt`. Otherwise it calls `create_account_payment`. `retryFailedPayment=true` sets the retry flag. `payOutstandingBalance` and `allInvoiceStatuses` are read only when feature flag `enable-eft-payment-method` is on, else False.
- `post_account` / `put_account`: return 202 if `cfs_account_id` is set and `cfs_account_status == PENDING`. Otherwise POST returns 201 and PUT returns 200. POST also needs `CREATE_SANDBOX_ACCOUNT` for sandbox requests.
- Fees (`fee.py`): `waiveFees` is honoured only if the JWT has STAFF. Otherwise `waive_fees=False`.
- EFT short names: the service lookup returns 404 when it finds nothing. `patch_eft_shortname_link` returns 404 if `link['short_name_id'] != short_name_id`. Refunds: `GET` and `POST /shortname-refund` need EFT_REFUND or EFT_REFUND_APPROVER. `PATCH` needs requires_auth and EFT_REFUND_APPROVER.
- FAS routing slips: a distinct role per route (FAS_CREATE, FAS_SEARCH, FAS_REPORTS, FAS_VIEW, FAS_EDIT, FAS_LINK). Search with no `page` in the body sets `return_all=True`. Comments accept either the `comment` schema or `comment_bcrs_schema`. FAS refund needs FAS_REFUND or FAS_REFUND_APPROVER and returns 202.
- Purchase history: `viewAll=true` needs `VIEW_ALL_TRANSACTIONS` and searches all accounts. Otherwise it needs `EDITOR` and searches that account. The report is a PDF if `Accept` is PDF, else CSV.
- `refund.py`: needs SYSTEM, CREATE_CREDITS or FAS_REFUND. An empty body is accepted.
- Distribution codes: all routes need `MANAGE_GL_CODES`. EFT short names need SYSTEM or MANAGE_EFT.

## Boundaries
- No auth at all (notes show none): `GET /codes/*`, `/fees/schedules`, `/meta/info`, `/ops/healthz` and `/ops/readyz`. `/ops/*` run `select 1` and return 500 on `SQLAlchemyError`.
- `post_transaction`, `patch_transaction` and `POST /payments/<id>/transactions` have no auth check in the notes.
- `patch_account`, `put_account` and `delete_account` show a SYSTEM role but no `@_jwt.requires_auth` in the notes.
- `post_account_fees`, `delete_account_fees` and `put_account_fee_product` have no `check_auth` call. They need only the MANAGE_ACCOUNTS role.
- `post_eft_shortname_link` is noted as lacking `@_jwt.requires_auth`. Its role check is present.
- Invoice `DELETE` and `PATCH`, receipts and `invoices.py` GET need only JWT. The notes show no ownership check on the invoice.
- `bank_accounts` calls `CFSService.validate_bank_account(request_json)`, which gets an OAuth token and POSTs to CFS with a Bearer token. The resource passes no credential itself. `BusinessException` and `ServiceUnavailableException` are returned as responses.
- Everywhere, `BusinessException` is caught and returned as `exception.response()`. Nothing is retried and nothing is recorded. Other exceptions propagate.

## Hazards
- No duplicate guards on invoice, refund, payment, link or comment creation. Repeated calls can duplicate work.
- `patch_routing_slip`'s `action` is unvalidated. Page and limit parsing is unvalidated too.
- Missing `requires_auth` on the routes listed above leaves them without the JWT decorator.
