## Role
Scheduled batch jobs (`jobs/payment-jobs`) for the BC Registries pay system. They run with no caller and no permission check. They read pay-db and Oracle (BCOL), then call CFS/PayBC/Direct Pay via pay-api services. They write CGI EJV/AP files to SFTP and minio, publish mailer, notify and lock events to a GCP queue, and move invoices, routing slips, CFS accounts and statements between states.

## Contract
- **In:** DB rows picked by status filters. Oracle `bconline_billing_record` (BCOL refunds). The Auth API (`AUTH_API_ENDPOINT orgs/{id}/contacts`, bearer token).
- **Out, CFS (`CFSService`):** `create_cfs_account(identifier, contact_info, receipt_method, payment_info, site_name, is_fas)` returns `account_number`, `party_number`, `site_number`, `payment_instrument_number`. Also `create_account_invoice`, `get_invoice`, `create_cfs_receipt`, `apply_receipt`, `reverse_rs_receipt_in_cfs`, `adjust_receipt_to_zero`, `reverse_invoice`.
- **Out, Direct Pay:** `DirectPayService().get_token()` then `OAuthService.get/post` to `{PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_BASE_URL}/paybc/payment/{REF}/{invoice_number}`. The POST body is `{'revenue':[{lineNumber, revenueAccount, revenueAmount}]}`.
- **Out, queue:** `utils/mailer.py` calls `gcp_queue_publisher.publish_to_queue`. Source is `PAY_JOBS`, topic is `ACCOUNT_MAILER_TOPIC`. Used by `publish_mailer_events`, `publish_statement_notification` and `publish_payment_notification`.
- **Out, notify:** `statement_notification_task.send_email` POSTs to `NOTIFY_API_ENDPOINT notify/` with a bearer token and `{recipients, subject, html_body}`. The body comes from `statement_notification.html`.
- **Out, files:** CGI files (`cgi_ejv.py`, `cgi_ap.py`) go to SFTP via `upload_to_ftp`, then to minio via `put_object`.

## Decisions (function / constant)
- `cfs_create_account_task.create_accounts`: CASH/CHEQUE goes to `routing_slip.create_cfs_account`; other methods go to `_create_cfs_account`.
- `_create_cfs_account`: EFT uses receipt method `CFS_RCPT_EFT_WIRE`. If cfs_account, party and site already exist, it calls `update_bank_details` and sets PAD. If bank, branch and account numbers exist, it creates the account with `RECEIPT_METHOD_PAD_DAILY` (PAD); otherwise `receipt_method=None`.
- Same function: status is `PENDING_PAD_ACTIVATION` if `pad_activation_date` is in the future, otherwise `ACTIVE`. A PAD failure that `_check_user_error` flags as a user error sets `INACTIVE` and publishes `PAD_SETUP_FAILED`.
- `activate_pad_account_task.activate_pad_accounts`: for `PENDING_PAD_ACTIVATION` accounts where `pad_activation_date - 1h < now`, sets the CFS account `ACTIVE`. If flag `multiple-payment-methods` is off, it also sets the payment method to PAD. Then it publishes `CONFIRMATION_PERIOD_OVER`.
- `cfs_create_invoice_task`: PAD, EFT, online-banking and routing-slip invoices are each created in CFS. Accounts with status `FREEZE` are excluded for PAD. Accounts not `ACTIVE`/`INACTIVE` are skipped. If `create_account_invoice` raises, it sleeps 10s and checks `get_invoice`. If the invoice is missing or the totals differ, it sends Sentry and skips. Online banking is skipped unless `corp_type.is_online_banking_allowed`. A successful online-banking invoice is set to `SETTLEMENT_SCHEDULED`.
- `routing_slip_task`:
  - `link_routing_slips` reverses the child receipt unless CFS status is `REV`, then creates the parent receipt.
  - `process_nsf`: reverses the receipt (NSF), sets the payment FAILED, freezes the account, resets invoices to CREATED and creates an NSF invoice (BCR/NSF fee).
  - `adjust_routing_slips`: for REFUND_AUTHORIZED or WRITE_OFF_AUTHORIZED with remaining_amount > 0, calls `adjust_receipt_to_zero`.
  - `process_correction` skips slips that have APPROVED/CREATED invoices.
  - `process_void` raises if the slip has invoices.
  - `apply_routing_slips_to_invoice` applies receipts per slip and breaks when `amount_due == 0`.
- `eft_task`:
  - `get_eft_credit_invoice_links_by_status` selects links by status: PENDING (APPROVED/OVERDUE invoices), PENDING_REFUND, CANCELLED.
  - `_create_receipt_and_invoice` raises `ValueError` if the CFS total differs from the invoice total.
  - `_rollback_receipt_and_invoice` and `_handle_invoice_refund` raise on consolidated invoice references.
  - `unlock_overdue_accounts` clears `has_overdue_invoices` when `InvoiceService.has_overdue_invoices` is false.
- `statement_task.generate_statements`: daily always. Weekly on Sunday (otherwise gap statements). Monthly on day 1. Notification status is PENDING only if `statement_notification_enabled` and there is no date override; otherwise SKIP. `_upsert_statements` reuses an existing statement matching account, frequency and dates.
- `statement_notification_task.send_notifications`: no recipients gives SKIP. EFT with the flag off gives SKIP. EFT with the flag on goes to `publish_statement_notification`. Other methods go to `send_email`.
- `statement_due_task`: `process_unpaid_statements` runs only if flag `enable-eft-payment-method` is on. `_update_invoice_overdue_status` sets EFT invoices in SETTLEMENT_SCHEDULED/PARTIAL/APPROVED with `overdue_date <= now` to OVERDUE. `_determine_action_and_due_date_by_invoice` returns OVERDUE, DUE (due day = `statement.to_date` + 1 month) or REMINDER (7 days before). Overdue action: lock event, then `add_to_non_sufficient_funds`.
- `ejv_payment_task`: government accounts (`stop_ejv` false/None, invoices APPROVED/REFUND_REQUESTED, method EJV, no ACTIVE reference). Batch GA means client == `CGI_BCREG_CLIENT_CODE`; GI means client != it. REFUND_REQUESTED reverses debit and credit; a reversal is skipped if it has no COMPLETED reference.
- `ejv_partner_distribution_task.get_invoices_for_disbursement`: PAID invoices, method not INTERNAL/DRAWDOWN/EFT, disbursement null or ERRORED, no receipt newer than `DISBURSEMENT_DELAY_IN_DAYS`, `corp_type_code == partner.code`. The refund-reversal variant takes REFUNDED/REFUND_REQUESTED/CREDITED invoices with disbursement COMPLETED.
- `ap_task.create_ap_files`: builds FAS routing-slip refund files (slips to REFUND_UPLOADED) and BCA non-gov disbursement files (invoices to UPLOADED). It uses batches of 250 and skips zero totals. `cgi_ap.py` branches on `ap_type`: REFUND gives CHQ and `CGI_AP_*` config; NON_GOV gives EFT and `BCA_*` config.
- `direct_pay_automated_refund_task`: reads the PayBC `refundglstatus`. Any RJCT/DECLINED gives `_refund_error`. All PAID with REFUND_REQUESTED gives REFUNDED. All CMPLT sets `gl_posted`.
- `distribution_task.update_failed_distributions`: for UPDATE_REVENUE_ACCOUNT and its _REFUND variant, a non-DIRECT_PAY invoice is finalised immediately. Otherwise, if any revenue line is PAID/RJCT (the GL post is not complete), it posts revenue lines first, then sets PAID or REFUNDED.
- `bcol_refund_confirmation_task._compare_and_update_records`: sets REFUNDED only if `invoice.total + bcol amount == 0`. A mismatch sends Sentry and skips; a missing record skips.
- `stale_payment_task`: transactions stale for 30 minutes are updated. A `COMPLETED_PAYMENT` error sets the transaction CANCELLED. Marked invoices are deleted. DIRECT_PAY invoices from the last 2 days with PayBC status PAID/CMPLT get their transaction updated.
- `unpaid_invoice_notify_task._notify_for_ob`: online-banking invoices (SETTLEMENT_SCHEDULED/PARTIAL/CREATED) created exactly `NOTIFY_AFTER_DAYS` ago get `PAYMENT_PENDING`.

## Boundaries
- No entry point has an auth check. All are job callers.
- Most tasks catch per account/invoice, send Sentry `capture_message(level='error')` and log, then continue. Exceptions: `cfs_bank_name_updater` (no handling), `ap_task` and `ejv_*` (errors propagate), `distribution_task` (no handling), and `stale_payment_task` (log only, no Sentry).
- `routing_slip.create_cfs_account` calls CFS with `is_fas=True` and the FAS token. On error it sends Sentry and rolls back, so the status stays unset.
- `cgi_ejv.upload_to_minio` swallows exceptions.
- Mailer functions return False/None on failure.
- None of the notes show retries or duplicate guards for CFS calls.

## Hazards
1. Money state can be committed before or without a later step. EFT receipts persist if `complete_post_invoice` fails. Overdue timestamps are saved before the lock event. `activate_pad_accounts` leaves the account ACTIVE if the publish fails.
2. No duplicate guard on CFS invoice, receipt or NSF invoice creation. The `get_invoice` recovery after a timeout can mask or repeat creation; concurrent runs can double-process.
3. Failures are silent or crash. A missing completed reference raises `IndexError` in the refund task. `_get_bca_distribution_string` has no null check. `apply_routing_slips_to_invoice` returns an error flag that callers only test for truthiness. The Direct Pay GET/POST calls have no error handling.

## Open first
- `tasks/cfs_create_invoice_task.py`: invoice creation for PAD, EFT, online-banking and routing-slip, with the 10s recovery.
- `tasks/routing_slip_task.py`: link, NSF, void, correction and receipt application.
- `tasks/eft_task.py`: EFT links, receipts and rollback.
- `utils/mailer.py` and `tasks/statement_due_task.py`: outbound queue messages and overdue and lock flow.

## Connections
- **[L1] `CFSService.create_cfs_account`** (pay-api): this part sends identifier, `{}` contact, `site_name=routing_slip.number` and `is_fas=True`. It gets back account, party and site numbers. The FAS profile class is chosen from `is_fas`. Bank details are saved only if `payment_info` is passed.
- **[L7] `OAuthService.get`**: used for the Auth contacts and Direct Pay GETs, with a bearer token. It raises `ServiceUnavailableException` on 5xx, and logs non-404 HTTP errors. The jobs never retry.
- **[L4] `DirectPayService`**: `get_token()` supplies the PayBC token for the refund and distribution tasks. `OrderStatus` here corresponds to its PayBC payment query response. `stale_payment_task` calls `DirectPayService.query_order_status`.
- **[L10] enums**: `PaymentDetailsGlStatus` is read from `pay_api.utils.enums`; `tasks/common/enums.py` also defines it.
- **[L2] `get_fiscal_year`**: the CGI batch header and trailer use it (fiscal year +1 if month > 3).
- **[L5] `cgi_reconciliations`**: the pay-queue feedback consumer for the EJV/AP files these jobs upload. Duplicate-feedback protection sits on its side (`feedback_file_ref`).
- **[L3] `eft_refund`**: `_handle_invoice_refund` is defined on the EFT task here, not in the pay-api refund service. The two do not call each other per the notes.
- **[L6] `DEFAULT_COUNTRY`**: read by `cfs_bank_name_updater`.
- **[L8], [L9] `EftService`**: `eft_task` and `cfs_create_invoice_task` call it; the notes for [L9] do not show its body.

structured.brief:
## Role
Shared frontend library layer of the BC Registries business-edit UI (Vue/Pinia): mixins, services and utils that components call. Services call the Auth API, Pay API and Legal API through the `@/axios-auth` axios instance, and read feature flags from LaunchDarkly. There is no server side here. The mixins are consumed by components; `mixin-tester.vue` composes AllowableActions, Common and Date mixins as a smoke test (empty template, no assertions). `schemas/office-address-schema.ts` is a Vuelidate schema re-exported for BaseAddress components.

## Contract
- In: component calls. Pinia getters: `getAllowedActions`, `getLegalType`, `isEntityCoop/Firm`, `isRoleStaff`, `getBusinessAddress`, `getRegisteredOfficeAddress`. `sessionStorage.BUSINESS_ID`. Feature flags.
- Out (all through `@/axios-auth`):
  - Auth API: `entities/{id}/authorizations`, `users/@me`, `entities/{id}`, `affiliationInvitations` (params `toOrgId`, `businessIdentifier`, `statuses=PENDING`), and PATCH `affiliationInvitations/{id}/authorization/{accept|refuse}` (no body).
  - Pay API: `codes/errors/{code}`, `accounts/{accountId}`.
  - Legal API (`LegalServices`): businesses, tasks, filings, addresses, parties (optional `?role=`), bootstrap filing, `nameRequests/{nr}/validate?phone&email`, comments, documents, and document blob download.
    - Writes: POST `businesses/{id}/filings?draft=true` with `{filing}`; POST `businesses?draft=true` with the business request; PUT `businesses/{id}/filings/{filingId}?draft=` with `{filing}`.
  - Digital credentials: `businesses/{id}/digitalCredentials` and its invitation, connections, `activeConnection`, `{credentialType}`, `{credentialId}/revoke` with `{reissue}` and delete routes. Also `documents/{file}/signatures` for a presigned URL, then PUT of the file to that URL with `Content-Type`, `x-amz-meta-userid`, `x-amz-meta-key` and `Content-Disposition` headers.
  - `DateUtilities.getServerDate`: HEAD `window.location.origin + VUE_APP_PATH`, reads the `Date` header.

## Decisions
- `AllowableActionsMixin.isAllowed(action)`: a switch over `AllowableActions`; most cases call private `isAllowedFiling(name, type)`, which looks in `getAllowedActions.filing.filingTypes` for a matching name (and subtype if given). Default is false.
  - Firms (`isEntityFirm`) map ADDRESS_CHANGE, DIRECTOR_CHANGE and BUSINESS_INFORMATION to CHANGE_OF_REGISTRATION. Coops with flag `special-resolution-ui-enabled` map BUSINESS_INFORMATION to SPECIAL_RESOLUTION. Others map it to ALTERATION.
  - Flags `supported-{dissolution,restoration,correction,put-back-on}-entities` must include `getLegalType`, else false. RESTORATION is true if FULL or LIMITED restoration is allowed.
  - BUSINESS_SUMMARY: flag list includes the legal type and `BUSINESS_ID` is in sessionStorage.
  - DETAIL_COMMENT and STAFF_COMMENT: `isBusiness && isRoleStaff`.
  - DIGITAL_CREDENTIALS: flag `enable-digital-credentials` and `getAllowedActions.digitalBusinessCard`.
  - `isGoodStanding` and `isEntitySoleProp` are read but unused.
- `CommonMixin.navigateToBusinessDashboard`: if flag `use-business-dashboard`, `navigate()` to `${getBusinessDashUrl}/${identifier}` (with `filing_id` if given); else `$router.push` to DASHBOARD, ignoring errors. `scrollToTop` skips when under Vitest. `validateAndScroll` scrolls to the first invalid component and returns false.
- `FilingMixin.updateFilingData`: removes the entry for the code, re-adds it only for 'add'. With an undefined code, it sets priority/waiveFees on all entries. `buildDissolutionFiling`: custodialOffice is the business address (or null) for SOLE_PROP/PARTNERSHIP, else the registered office address; type is always VOLUNTARY. `buildCorrectionFiling` sets an empty comment.
- `ResourceLookupMixin.directorWarning`: pushes alerts for these three conditions and returns the first, or null.
  - bcResident: all directors outside BC. The notes' condition is ambiguous.
  - canadianResident: more than 50% of directors have a non-CA address.
  - minDirectors: fewer non-ceased directors than the configured count.
- `EnumUtilities`: status and type predicates compare `item.status` or `item.name`. Subtype predicates also accept `item.<amalgamationApplication|dissolution|restoration>.type`. `isTypeStaff` is true for admin freeze, court order, administrative dissolution, put back on, registrar's notation or order. `filingTypeToName` maps types to display names ('Unknown Type' if falsy, `camelCaseToWords` fallback).
- `DateUtilities`: `yyyyMmDdToDate`, `formatYyyyMmDd` and `yyyyMmDdToApi` return null unless the string is 10 chars long. `compareYyyyMmDd` returns true if any argument is missing. Pacific time (America/Vancouver) is used throughout. `date-mixin` is a deprecated pass-through to it.
- `LegalServices` throws if the expected field is missing from the response ('Invalid business info', 'Invalid filings list', 'Invalid filing', 'Invalid comments', 'Invalid documents'). `fetchNameRequest`: 404 returns null; 400 and 403 throw. `fetchDocument` throws if `link` or `filename` is missing. `hasPendingTasks`: true if any task's filing status is not NEW.
- `GetFeatureFlag`: returns `defaultFlagSet[name]` when no LD client, else `ldClient.variation(name)`. `InitLdClient` needs `window.ldClientId`.

## Boundaries and failures
- None of the entry points shows an authorization check; the UI gating is only `isAllowed`/`isRoleStaff`.
- Auth API: only `fetchUserInfo` logs a falsy response, and it returns the data anyway. The other Auth calls have no handling and errors propagate.
- Pay API: `getPayErrorObj` swallows errors and returns undefined. `fetchCfsAccountId` logs and re-raises.
- Digital-credential and task helpers in `legal-services` catch every error, log it to the console and return null. Callers can't tell network, auth and server errors apart.
- `UpdateLdUser` swallows identify errors. A failed `InitLdClient` closes the client, and flags then fall back to defaults.
- `getServerDate` falls back silently to the browser date.

## Hazards
1. `compareYyyyMmDd` uses `eval()` on the operator and does no validation.
2. The null returns in the credential/task helpers make `hasPendingTasks` and others fail silently. `hasPendingTasks` has no null guard.
3. `getServerDate` silently falls back to the browser clock, which shifts date logic. The `getPayErrorObj` swallow hides payment error details.

## Open first
- `src/mixins/allowable-actions-mixin.ts`: all UI permission rules.
- `src/services/legal-services.ts`: Legal API client and digital credentials.
- `src/services/enum-utilities.ts`: status/type predicates and filing names.
- `src/utils/feature-flags.ts`: LD client and default flags.

## Connections

## Role
Shared frontend library layer of the BC Registries business-edit UI (Vue/Pinia): mixins, services and utils that components call. Services call the Auth API, Pay API and Legal API through the `@/axios-auth` axios instance, and read feature flags from LaunchDarkly. There is no server side here. The mixins are consumed by components; `mixin-tester.vue` composes AllowableActions, Common and Date mixins as a smoke test (empty template, no assertions). `schemas/office-address-schema.ts` is a Vuelidate schema re-exported for BaseAddress components.

## Contract
- In: component calls. Pinia getters: `getAllowedActions`, `getLegalType`, `isEntityCoop/Firm`, `isRoleStaff`, `getBusinessAddress`, `getRegisteredOfficeAddress`. `sessionStorage.BUSINESS_ID`. Feature flags.
- Out (all through `@/axios-auth`):
  - Auth API: `entities/{id}/authorizations`, `users/@me`, `entities/{id}`, `affiliationInvitations` (params `toOrgId`, `businessIdentifier`, `statuses=PENDING`), and PATCH `affiliationInvitations/{id}/authorization/{accept|refuse}` (no body).
  - Pay API: `codes/errors/{code}`, `accounts/{accountId}`.
  - Legal API (`LegalServices`): businesses, tasks, filings, addresses, parties (optional `?role=`), bootstrap filing, `nameRequests/{nr}/validate?phone&email`, comments, documents, and document blob download.
    - Writes: POST `businesses/{id}/filings?draft=true` with `{filing}`; POST `businesses?draft=true` with the business request; PUT `businesses/{id}/filings/{filingId}?draft=` with `{filing}`.
  - Digital credentials: `businesses/{id}/digitalCredentials` and its invitation, connections, `activeConnection`, `{credentialType}`, `{credentialId}/revoke` with `{reissue}` and delete routes. Also `documents/{file}/signatures` for a presigned URL, then PUT of the file to that URL with `Content-Type`, `x-amz-meta-userid`, `x-amz-meta-key` and `Content-Disposition` headers.
  - `DateUtilities.getServerDate`: HEAD `window.location.origin + VUE_APP_PATH`, reads the `Date` header.

## Decisions
- `AllowableActionsMixin.isAllowed(action)`: a switch over `AllowableActions`; most cases call private `isAllowedFiling(name, type)`, which looks in `getAllowedActions.filing.filingTypes` for a matching name (and subtype if given). Default is false.
  - Firms (`isEntityFirm`) map ADDRESS_CHANGE, DIRECTOR_CHANGE and BUSINESS_INFORMATION to CHANGE_OF_REGISTRATION. Coops with flag `special-resolution-ui-enabled` map BUSINESS_INFORMATION to SPECIAL_RESOLUTION. Others map it to ALTERATION.
  - Flags `supported-{dissolution,restoration,correction,put-back-on}-entities` must include `getLegalType`, else false. RESTORATION is true if FULL or LIMITED restoration is allowed.
  - BUSINESS_SUMMARY: flag list includes the legal type and `BUSINESS_ID` is in sessionStorage.
  - DETAIL_COMMENT and STAFF_COMMENT: `isBusiness && isRoleStaff`.
  - DIGITAL_CREDENTIALS: flag `enable-digital-credentials` and `getAllowedActions.digitalBusinessCard`.
  - `isGoodStanding` and `isEntitySoleProp` are read but unused.
- `CommonMixin.navigateToBusinessDashboard`: if flag `use-business-dashboard`, `navigate()` to `${getBusinessDashUrl}/${identifier}` (with `filing_id` if given); else `$router.push` to DASHBOARD, ignoring errors. `scrollToTop` skips when under Vitest. `validateAndScroll` scrolls to the first invalid component and returns false.
- `FilingMixin.updateFilingData`: removes the entry for the code, re-adds it only for 'add'. With an undefined code, it sets priority/waiveFees on all entries. `buildDissolutionFiling`: custodialOffice is the business address (or null) for SOLE_PROP/PARTNERSHIP, else the registered office address; type is always VOLUNTARY. `buildCorrectionFiling` sets an empty comment.
- `ResourceLookupMixin.directorWarning`: pushes alerts for these three conditions and returns the first, or null.
  - bcResident: all directors outside BC. The notes' condition is ambiguous.
  - canadianResident: more than 50% of directors have a non-CA address.
  - minDirectors: fewer non-ceased directors than the configured count.
- `EnumUtilities`: status and type predicates compare `item.status` or `item.name`. Subtype predicates also accept `item.<amalgamationApplication|dissolution|restoration>.type`. `isTypeStaff` is true for admin freeze, court order, administrative dissolution, put back on, registrar's notation or order. `filingTypeToName` maps types to display names ('Unknown Type' if falsy, `camelCaseToWords` fallback).
- `DateUtilities`: `yyyyMmDdToDate`, `formatYyyyMmDd` and `yyyyMmDdToApi` return null unless the string is 10 chars long. `compareYyyyMmDd` returns true if any argument is missing. Pacific time (America/Vancouver) is used throughout. `date-mixin` is a deprecated pass-through to it.
- `LegalServices` throws if the expected field is missing from the response ('Invalid business info', 'Invalid filings list', 'Invalid filing', 'Invalid comments', 'Invalid documents'). `fetchNameRequest`: 404 returns null; 400 and 403 throw. `fetchDocument` throws if `link` or `filename` is missing. `hasPendingTasks`: true if any task's filing status is not NEW.
- `GetFeatureFlag`: returns `defaultFlagSet[name]` when no LD client, else `ldClient.variation(name)`. `InitLdClient` needs `window.ldClientId`.

## Boundaries and failures
- None of the entry points shows an authorization check; the UI gating is only `isAllowed`/`isRoleStaff`.
- Auth API: only `fetchUserInfo` logs a falsy response, and it returns the data anyway. The other Auth calls have no handling and errors propagate.
- Pay API: `getPayErrorObj` swallows errors and returns undefined. `fetchCfsAccountId` logs and re-raises.
- Digital-credential and task helpers in `legal-services` catch every error, log it to the console and return null. Callers can't tell network, auth and server errors apart.
- `UpdateLdUser` swallows identify errors. A failed `InitLdClient` closes the client, and flags then fall back to defaults.
- `getServerDate` falls back silently to the browser date.

## Hazards
1. `compareYyyyMmDd` uses `eval()` on the operator and does no validation.
2. The null returns in the credential/task helpers make `hasPendingTasks` and others fail silently. `hasPendingTasks` has no null guard.
3. `getServerDate` silently falls back to the browser clock, which shifts date logic. The `getPayErrorObj` swallow hides payment error details.

## Open first
- `src/mixins/allowable-actions-mixin.ts`: all UI permission rules.
- `src/services/legal-services.ts`: Legal API client and digital credentials.
- `src/services/enum-utilities.ts`: status/type predicates and filing names.
- `src/utils/feature-flags.ts`: LD client and default flags.

## Connections
- [L12] `App.vue` calls `getServerDate` (date service) and `AuthServices.fetchAuthorizations`, `fetchUserInfo` and `fetchEntityInfo`, plus the `LegalServices` fetches. It throws if there is no auth role. This part adds no checks.
- [L7], [L8], [L9] `TodoList.vue` calls `PayServices.getPayErrorObj(getPayApiUrl, paymentStatusCode)` when a status code exists. This part swallows errors and returns undefined, so TodoList sees no error; its handling isn't shown. TodoList also calls `AuthServices.fetchAffiliationInvitations` (it catches errors and shows a dialog) and uses `apiToDate`/`daysFromToday`.
- [L11] `StandaloneDirectorsFiling.vue` calls `hasFilingCode` from `FilingMixin`, and uses `navigateToBusinessDashboard`.
- [L6], [L10] `OfficeAddresses.vue` passes `officeAddressSchema` to BaseAddress; the notes show no further check.
- [L2], [L3] legal-api `is_allowed` / `check_authorization` is the server-side counterpart to `isAllowed`. The notes show no shared source: the client check reads `getAllowedActions`, while the server checks `authorized(... ['edit'])` and `is_allowed` on its own. A UI allow therefore doesn't bypass the server.

**Note:** the claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive MCP servers need authorization (claude.ai connector settings, or `/mcp` in an interactive session). They are unavailable until then. This summary did not need them.

## Role
The legal-api Flask REST layer. It wires the v1 and v2 route trees, version-based redirects, and the v2 admin, meta and request-tracker resources. It takes HTTP calls from staff and admin UIs. It hands work to NATS subjects (entity events, emailer, filer), to namex, and to the local DB (Configuration, Review, RequestTracker).

## Contract
- **Routing:** `endpoints.py` registers `API_BLUEPRINT` (v1), `OPS_BLUEPRINT`, and v2 via `v2_endpoint.init_app`. `V2Endpoint.init_app` (`v2/__init__.py`) registers meta, admin, businesses, digital_credentials, document, namerequest, naics, request_tracker, internal and mras blueprints.
- **Entity event:** `publish_entity_event` (`admin/administrative_bn.py`) sends `queue.publish_json(payload, NATS_ENTITY_EVENT_SUBJECT)`. The payload has `specversion='1.x-wip'`, `type='bc.registry.admin.bn'`, `datacontenttype='application/json'`, and `message_id` (a uuid4 if not supplied). `request_name` is `BN15` from the admin endpoint and `RESUBMIT_<requestType>` from request_tracker. The entity-bn processors consume this event.
- **Emailer:** `{'email': {'filingId', 'type': filing_type, 'option': filing.status}}` on `NATS_EMAILER_SUBJECT`.
- **Filer:** `{'filing': {'id'}}` on `NATS_FILER_SUBJECT`.
- **Namex:** `namex.query_nr_numbers(nr_numbers)` returns JSON objects with `nrNum` and `expirationDate`.

## Decisions
- **Version routing**
  - `before_request`: with `accept-version` V1, an `API.` endpoint is redirected to `API_V1.`. With V2, an `API.` endpoint that doesn't already start with `API_V2.` is redirected to `API_V2.`.
  - `_handle_api_error` (404/405): a path under `/api/v2` is redirected to `/api/v1`. A bare `/api` path with neither 'v1' nor 'v2' is redirected to v1.
  - `_redirect`: an OPTIONS request gets the default response with CORS headers (`*`, `Authorization, Content-Type`).
- **Admin BN** (`POST /bn/<identifier>[/<business_number>]`): no business found returns 400 'A valid business is required.'. Otherwise it publishes, then returns 201.
- **Configuration** (staff)
  - GET: `names` is split on commas and uppercased. An empty list gives 400, and no matches gives 404.
  - PUT: `validate_configurations` rejects an empty list ('Configurations list cannot be empty'), duplicate names ('Duplicate names error.') and unknown names, comparing the found count with the requested count ('Invalid name error.'). It also rejects NUM_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED > MAX_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED, using the DB value for whichever is missing from the payload.
  - PUT: `validate_data_types` calls `Configuration.validate_configuration_value`. A ValueError during the update triggers rollback and returns 400. Values are stored as `str(value)` in one commit.
- **Reviews** (staff)
  - GET list: for statuses CHANGE_REQUESTED, AWAITING_REVIEW and RESUBMITTED, it adds NR expiry dates via `get_expiry_date_for_each_nr`.
  - POST `/reviews/<id>`: review not found gives 404. Review status not AWAITING_REVIEW or RESUBMITTED gives 400 'No changes allowed.'. Missing status gives 'Status is required.'. A status outside CHANGE_REQUESTED, APPROVED and REJECTED gives 'Invalid Status.'. CHANGE_REQUESTED or REJECTED without a comment gives 'Comment is required.'.
  - POST order: create `ReviewResult` (reviewer_id, status, comments), append it and save the review, call `filing.set_review_decision()`, publish to emailer, then publish to filer only if `filing.status == APPROVED` and `effective_date <= now(UTC)`.
- **Request tracker** (`admin_edit` or `bn_edit`)
  - GET `/bn/<identifier>` excludes `GET_BN` records. Both GET and POST `/bn/<identifier>` return 400 if the business is not found.
  - POST saves a `RequestTracker` (`retry_number=-1`, `is_admin=True`, `BN_HUB`), then publishes the event.
- **Dissolution stats** (staff): `get_statistics` returns `{'data': {'eligibleCount': ...}}` from `InvoluntaryDissolutionService.get_businesses_eligible_count()`.

## Boundaries
- **Guards:** admin BN uses `jwt.has_one_of_roles([admin_edit, bn_edit])`. request_tracker's three routes require admin_edit or bn_edit. Configuration, reviews and dissolution statistics use `has_one_of_roles([staff])`.
- **No guards:** `endpoints.py` has no auth on any route or handler. `meta.py` `/api/v2/meta/info` has none.
- **Errors:** `publish_entity_event` catches everything, sends it to Sentry, logs it and re-raises, so the endpoint fails. It does not retry.
- **Absent checks:** the notes show no try/except around namex, the queue publishes, `RequestTracker.save()` or the enum lookup. They show no idempotency guard on BN requests or `ReviewResult`, and no validation of `business_number` or the request body.

## Hazards
1. Reviews POST saves the review result before publishing. A failed emailer or filer publish leaves the decision committed with no notification or filing. No retry is shown.
2. request_tracker POST saves the record, then publishes. A publish failure leaves a tracker with `retry_number=-1` and no event. A bad `requestType` raises an unhandled KeyError. GET `/<request_tracker_id>` does not check for None.
3. Configuration PUT calls `Configuration.find_by_name` without a None check, so a missing name raises AttributeError, which the code does not catch (it only catches ValueError).

## Open first
- `resources/v2/admin/reviews.py`: review decision flow and queue publishes.
- `resources/v2/request_tracker.py` and `admin/administrative_bn.py`: BN resubmission and the event publish.
- `resources/v2/admin/configuration.py`: validation of config updates.
- `resources/endpoints.py`: version redirects and blueprint wiring.

## Connections
- **[L1] colin-api `API_BLUEPRINT`:** same name and a '/api/v1' prefix, but a different service's blueprint. The notes show no link to this part's `/api/v1` blueprint.
- **[L2] bcol-api `API_BLUEPRINT`:** same as L1, a different service.
- **[L3] business-pay `pay_filer`:** shares `queue.publish_json` only as a name. This part publishes with subjects from its own config. The notes show no other link.
- **[L4] pay-api `EndpointEnum`:** the redirect logic here uses `EndpointEnum` (API, API_V1, API_V2, with values '/api', '/api/v1', '/api/v2'). The L4 notes list only API_V1 '/api/v1', API '/api', TEST_API and DEFAULT_API. API_V2 is not in them.
- **[L5] auth-web `ContinuationAuthorizationReview.vue`:** the UI submits a review result with a status and comments. That matches the POST `/reviews/<id>` payload checks here. The UI shows the form only for AWAITING_REVIEW or RESUBMITTED, which matches the server's 'No changes allowed.' check. The server re-validates independently.
- **[L6] entity-filer config:** defines `NATS_ENTITY_EVENT_SUBJECT` (default 'entity.events'), NATS_EMAILER_SUBJECT and NATS_FILER_SUBJECT. The entity event, emailer and filer publishes here read the same-named keys from this app's own config. The notes don't show that the two configs hold the same values.
- **[L8]/[L9] business-pay `ReviewStatus`:** the enum (AWAITING_REVIEW, CHANGE_REQUESTED, RESUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED) matches the statuses checked in reviews.py.
- **[L10]/[L11]/[L12] entity-bn processors:** they create and update `RequestTracker` records (INFORM_CRA, GET_BN, CHANGE_STATUS) with retry counts. The request_tracker POST here creates `retry_number=-1` records with `is_admin=True` and publishes `RESUBMIT_<type>` for entity-bn to pick up. L12's `process` uses `is_admin` to take the business number from `msg.data.header.businessNumber`. Since administrative_bn does not validate `business_number`, an unchecked value can reach the BN Hub path. The notes show no admin check on the entity-bn side.

OPS_BLUEPRINT at '/ops' exposes OPS_API for operational health. API_BLUEPRINT at '/api/v1' exposes nine domain namespaces at their respective paths. --- [L3] lear/queue_services/business-pay/src/business_pay/resources/pay_filer.py, in "business-pay queue service"
Link: this part sends `queue.publish_json` (shares there): Publishes JSON payload to NATS subject; credentials from current_app.config.
Processes cloud event messages containing filing payments: receives payment completion events, marks filings as paid, triggers staff review or publishes to filer queue, and notifies emailer. ENTRY: POST /worker() - callable by any client with valid GCP JWT token; checks `verify_gcp_jwt(request)` returns falsy (no error), else returns 403 FORBIDDEN. RULE: if `not request.data` -> return 200 OK, drop from queue. RULE: if cloud event not obtained or not instance of SimpleCloudEvent -> return 200 OK, drop from queue (in worker). RULE: if `payment_token.status_code != "COMPLETED"` -> return 200 OK, drop from queue. RULE: if `payment_token.corp_type_code in ["MHR", "BTR"]` -> return 200 OK, drop from queue. RULE: if filing not found AND `payment_token.filing_identifier == None` AND `payment_token.corp_type_code == "BC"` -> return 200 OK, drop from queue (in worker). RULE: if filing not found AND above condition false -> return 404 NOT_FOUND, put back on queue. RULE: if `filing.payment_completion_date` already set -> return 200 OK, drop from queue. RULE: if `filing.filing_type in ["continuationIn"]` -> create_staff_review(filing); else publish_to_filer(filing, payment_token). RULE: in publish_to_filer, if `filing.effective_date <= filing.payment_completion_date` -> publish to filer queue; else skip publish (in worker). ORDER: Sets filing.payment_completion_date, filing.payment_status_code, filing.status, calls filing.save(); then branches to create_staff_review or publish_to_filer; then publish_to_emailer; all three final steps wrapped with `suppress(Exception)` so exceptions logged but swallowed, later steps still run. ON ERROR: publish_to_filer wraps entire logic …

Resource for managing statement notification settings in a payment API account.

ENTRY: POST /accounts/<account_id>/statements/notifications - requires JWT auth, checks user has CHANGE_STATEMENT_SETTINGS role and is_premium=True for the account.

RULE: StatementRecipients.update_statement_notification_details raises BusinessException -> returns exception.response(), in `post_account_notification`.

ON ERROR: BusinessException caught, returns its response() output; all other errors unhandled.

CALLS OUT: StatementRecipients.find_statement_notification_details(account_id) - retrieves notification details.

CALLS OUT: StatementRecipients.update_statement_notification_details(account_id, request_json) - updates notification settings with request payload.

## Role
The legal-api REST layer (Flask-RESTX v1 namespaces plus a few v2 blueprints) for business entities. It reads business data (addresses, aliases, directors, resolutions, share classes, comments, tasks, filings) from the datastore and creates, updates and deletes filings. It hands work to the payment service (invoice create/cancel/status), namex (name requests), MinIO (file deletion), the filing queue (`queue.publish_json`), and `RegistrationBootstrapService`. The COLIN service calls the internal endpoints.

## Contract
- **Mounts:** `/ops`, `/api/v1/meta`, `/api/v1/businesses`, `/api/v1/documents`, `/api/v1/nameRequests`, `/api/v1/nrTypeMap`. The v2 blueprints are `API2` at `/api/v2/businesses` and `ADMIN_V2` at `/api/v2/admin`; the admin blueprint has no routes here. Namespaces declare `security=['apikey']`, but the notes show no check of the key value.
- **Filings:** `/<identifier>/filings[/<filing_id>]` take GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, with CORS `*`. A temp identifier starts with `T`; NR identifiers start with `NR`.
- **Queue:** `queue.publish_json({'filing': {'id': filing.id}})`.
- **Payment POST** (`ListFilingResource._create_invoice`): to `PAYMENT_SVC_URL` with `Bearer <user jwt>`, timeout 20s. Body: `{businessInfo:{businessIdentifier,corpType,businessName,contactInfo}, filingInfo:{filingTypes}, [folioNumber], [accountInfo:{routingSlip|bcolAccountNumber|datNumber}]}`.
- **Internal:** `/internal/filings[/<status>]`, `PATCH /internal/filings/<id>`, `/internal/filings/colin_id[/<id>]` and `/internal/tax_ids` serve COLIN.

## Decisions
- **Filing creation:** `business.post` accepts only `incorporationApplication` or `registration`. It calls `RegistrationBootstrapService.create_bootstrap`, then `register_bootstrap`, then `ListFilingResource.put`. A failed step returns 503, and a failed register deletes the bootstrap inside `suppress(Exception)`.
- **PUT:** `put` validates, then `_save_filing`, then `complete_filing`. Draft or `only_validate` returns early. It skips validation for historical COLIN filings (`_is_historical_colin_filing`: source COLIN and date before `BOB_DATE`) and before-epoch filings (`_is_before_epoch_filing`).
- **`_check_authorization`:** returns 401 unless `authorized(identifier, jwt, ['edit'])` and `is_allowed(...)` both pass.
- **`complete_filing`:** `_check_and_update_nr`, then `_create_invoice`, then `_set_effective_date`, with COLIN handled in `_process_colin_filing`.
- **`_process_colin_filing`:** an epoch filing before the epoch sets the transaction id and `set_processed`. Otherwise it publishes to the queue. A filing with no `colin_event_ids` gets 400.
- **Fee codes:** `_get_filing_types` builds the codes. Special cases are correction, voluntary dissolution, COOP extras, and `changeOfDirectors` "free" when all actions are name or address changes.
- **`_create_invoice` results:** 200/201 stores `payment_token`, status, account and roles on the filing. 400 stores the error type. Anything else, or a connection error or timeout, returns 402 `unable to create invoice for payment.`
- **Effective dates:** `_set_effective_date` uses `futureEffectiveDate` for incorporation and registration. A non-COOP `changeOfAddress` gets tomorrow 00:01.
- **DELETE:** if `filing.deletion_locked`, `_create_deletion_locked_response` returns 401. Otherwise it deletes, and for `T` identifiers it calls `deregister_bootstrap` and `delete_bootstrap`.
- **MinIO cleanup:** `_delete_from_minio` removes rules/memorandum keys (incorporationApplication, alteration), `affidavitFileKey` (dissolution) and `fileKey` (courtOrder).
- **PATCH:** first `requests.delete` on `{PAYMENT_SVC_URL}/{payment_token}` (timeout 20, Bearer), then `reset_filing_to_draft()` only if the status is 200 or 202. A connection error or timeout returns 500.
- **GET filing:** `get` returns only COMPLETED and PAID filings in list mode. For a PENDING filing it fetches payment status and adds `isPaymentActionRequired` and `paymentMethod`; a connection error or timeout is logged and skipped. A PDF is returned only for `amalgamationApplication`, `incorporationApplication` and `continuationIn`.
- **Tasks:** `business_tasks.get` handles NR identifiers through `namex.query_nr_number` and `validate_nr`, returning 403 if not consumable. It fetches payment details for filings with `payment_status_code == 'CREATED'`, and a connection error returns 503.
- **Comments:** posts require `authorized(..., ['add_comment'])`, `validate(json, ...)` and `Comment.save()`. For filing comments, `json_input['comment']['filingId']` must equal `filing_id`, and `filing.business_id` must equal `business.id`.
- **NR proxy v2:** `validate_with_contact_info` returns the NR if `AccountService.get_account_by_affiliated_identifier` returns any orgs. Otherwise it needs email or phone (403 if neither) and string-compares them to the applicant (400 on mismatch).
- **`nr_type_map`:** filters the mapping tuples by `nrTypeCd`, `entityTypeCd` and `requestActionCd`, returning 404 if none match. One chunk shows an unimplemented filter, so treat that as unclear.

## Boundaries
- **GET views:** `business`, `business_address`, `business_directors`, `business_resolutions`, `business_share_classes` (v1 and v2) and `business.get` (non-`T` identifiers; `T` returns a 200 message) use `@jwt.requires_auth`. They also use `authorized(identifier, jwt, ['view'])`, which returns 401 after the 404 business check. The notes do not give what `authorized` compares.
- **Delete:** `delete` needs `authorized(..., ['edit'])`.
- **No role or auth check:** aliases, `namerequest` v1 and v2, `nrTypeMap`, `meta`, and the GET handlers of `/internal/filings` and `colin_id`. `business_comments.get` has only the JWT decorator, and `filing_comments.get` is JWT-only as well (the note says no `authorized` call on get).
- **COLIN role:** `jwt.validate_roles([COLIN_SVC_ROLE])` guards `InternalFilings.patch`, `ColinLastUpdate.post`, and GET/POST `/internal/tax_ids`, which return 401 without it.
- **Committed before a failable step:** `_create_invoice` saves the filing before it returns. `_save_filing` saves before payment. `tax_ids` POST saves per identifier.
- **Failure handling:** payment, namex and queue calls have no retry. Errors are logged or returned, not recorded for later.

## Hazards
1. `put` has a bare `except Exception` around `_save_filing` that prints and still calls `complete_filing`. Invoice creation can then run on an unsaved filing.
2. `ColinLastUpdate.post` builds its SQL insert by interpolating the raw `colin_id` (injection risk). `InternalFilings.patch` also appends `ColinEventId` rows with no duplicate check.
3. `queue.publish_json` has no retry. `bootstrap.delete()` failures are swallowed, so orphan bootstraps are possible. The GET filing payment fetch has no timeout.

## Open first
- `resources/v1/business/business_filings.py`: filing CRUD, invoice creation, effective dates, COLIN processing, internal filings.
- `resources/v1/business/business.py`: bootstrap-based incorporation and registration creation.
- `resources/v1/business/internal_services.py`: COLIN tax-id endpoints.
- `resources/v2/namerequest.py`: contact-info validation of NRs.

## Connections
- **[L12] pay-api `PaymentService`:** this part POSTs the invoice payload with the caller's Bearer JWT. Success is 200/201 with `id`, `statusCode` and `isPaymentActionRequired`; failure is 400 with `type` and `detail`. The payment service therefore sees the end user's token, not a service credential.
- **[L4] business-pay `pay_filer`:** it takes the payment-complete event and sets the filing status, then publishes to the filer queue. This part publishes `{'filing':{'id'}}` for COLIN processing. The notes show no shared message-shape check.
- **[L3] `allowable-actions-mixin.ts`:** the UI decides allowed actions client-side. The server enforces only `authorized` and `is_allowed`, and the notes show no tie between the two.
- **[L6]–[L11] UI views:** `saveFiling` POSTs and PUTs filings here. A 402 from invoice failure shows the payment error dialog. Filings are saved before the invoice, so a draft can exist after a 402.
- **[L1], [L2] and [L5]:** other services' app factories and a pay-api utility, with no connection to these endpoints beyond sharing names.

--- [L1] lear/colin-api/src/colin_api/__init__.py, in "COLIN API (colin-api)"
Link: it receives `API_BLUEPRINT` here: Blueprint with API routes, registered on the Flask app
Flask application factory for Colin API (Legal Entity System).

create_app(run_mode=os.getenv('FLASK_ENV', 'production')) constructs Flask app from CONFIGURATION[run_mode]; conditionally initializes Sentry with dsn=app.config.get('SENTRY_DSN'); initializes flags service; registers error handlers on API; registers API_BLUEPRINT and OPS_BLUEPRINT; calls setup_jwt_manager(); adds after_request hook appending response.headers['API'] with colin_api/{version} from get_run_version().

Helper setup_jwt_manager(app, jwt_manager) sets app.config['JWT_ROLE_CALLBACK'] to extract realm_access.roles and init_app(app).

Helper register_shellcontext(app) registers app and jwt in shell.

Entry point create_app: this chunk shows no check. Logging setup runs on module import.

--- [L2] sbc-pay/bcol-api/src/bcol_api/__init__.py, in "bcol-api: BCOL payment/profile gateway"
Link: it receives `API_BLUEPRINT` here: registered to the app; contains API routes
Flask application factory for the BCOL payment API service.

Entry point: create_app(run_mode) loads configuration by run_mode (defaults to FLASK_ENV env var or 'production'). Flow: creates Flask app, loads config from config.CONFIGURATION[run_mode], conditionally initializes Sentry if SENTRY_ENABLE == 'true' (string) and SENTRY_DSN is set, registers API_BLUEPRINT and OPS_BLUEPRINT, applies convert_to_camel after_request converter, calls setup_jwt_manager() to configure JWT with get_roles callback extracting realm_access.roles from token, registers ExceptionHandler, adds after_request hook add_version() setting API header to bcol_api/{version}, registers shell context with app and jwt. This chunk shows no check on create_app entry point; config loading may fail if run_mode not in CONFIGURATION dict.

--- [L3] business-filings-ui/src/mixins/allowable-actions-mixin.ts, in "Shared client-side support layer (mixins, services, utils)"
Link: this part sends `is_allowed` (defined there): Checks if filing is allowed given business state, filing type, legal type, JWT, filing subtype, filing_id
A Vue mixin that determines which business filing actions and filings are permitted for the current user and entity, used by the BC Registries filing system to show/hide UI options. ENTRY: `isAllowed(action: AllowableActions)` — no check in this chunk; called by parent component to test if an action is allowed. ENTRY: `isAllowedFiling(name: FilingTypes, type: FilingSubTypes = null)` — private; called only by `isAllowed`. RULE: ADDRESS_CHANGE — if isEntityFirm → check CHANGE_OF_REGISTRATION allowed; else → check CHANGE_OF_ADDRESS allowed. RULE: ADMINISTRATIVE_DISSOLUTION — if feature flag 'supported-dissolution-entities' includes getLegalType → check DISSOLUTION + DISSOLUTION_ADMINISTRATIVE allowed; else → false. RULE: AGM_EXTENSION — check AGM_EXTENSION allowed. RULE: AGM_LOCATION_CHANGE — check AGM_LOCATION_CHANGE allowed. RULE: AMALGAMATION — check AMALGAMATION_APPLICATION allowed. RULE: AMALGAMATION_OUT — check AMALGAMATION_OUT allowed. RULE: ANNUAL_REPORT — check ANNUAL_REPORT allowed. RULE: BUSINESS_INFORMATION — if isEntityCoop and feature flag 'special-resolution-ui-enabled' → check SPECIAL_RESOLUTION allowed; else if isEntityFirm → check CHANGE_OF_REGISTRATION allowed; else → check ALTERATION allowed. RULE: BUSINESS_SUMMARY — if feature flag 'supported-business-summary-entities' includes getLegalType and isBusiness (sessionStorage.BUSINESS_ID exists) → true; else → false. RULE: CONSENT_AMALGAMATION_OUT — check CONSENT_AMALGAMATION_OUT allowed. RULE: CONSENT_CONTINUATION_OUT — check CONSENT_CONTINUATION_OUT allowed. RULE: CONTINUATION_OUT — check CONTINUATION_OUT allowed. RULE: CORRECTION — if feature flag 'supported-correction-entities' includes getLegalType → check CORRECTION allowed; else → false. RULE: COURT_ORDER — check COURT_ORDER allowed. RULE: DETAIL_COMMENT — if isBusiness and isRoleStaff → true; else → false. …

--- [L4] lear/queue_services/business-pay/src/business_pay/resources/pay_filer.py, in "business-pay queue service"
Link: this part sends `queue.publish_json` (shares there): Publishes {'filing': {'id': filing.id}} payload to queue for post-processing
Processes cloud event messages containing filing payments: receives payment completion events, marks filings as paid, triggers staff review or publishes to filer queue, and notifies emailer. ENTRY: POST /worker() - callable by any client with valid GCP JWT token; checks `verify_gcp_jwt(request)` returns falsy (no error), else returns 403 FORBIDDEN. RULE: if `not request.data` -> return 200 OK, drop from queue. RULE: if cloud event not obtained or not instance of SimpleCloudEvent -> return 200 OK, drop from queue (in worker). RULE: if `payment_token.status_code != "COMPLETED"` -> return 200 OK, drop from queue. RULE: if `payment_token.corp_type_code in ["MHR", "BTR"]` -> return 200 OK, drop from queue. RULE: if filing not found AND `payment_token.filing_identifier == None` AND `payment_token.corp_type_code == "BC"` -> return 200 OK, drop from queue (in worker). RULE: if filing not found AND above condition false -> return 404 NOT_FOUND, put back on queue. RULE: if `filing.payment_completion_date` already set -> return 200 OK, drop from queue. structured.brief:
## business-pay (queue service)

Flask worker that receives GCP Pub/Sub push events for completed filing payments, marks the Filing paid in the shared DB, then either creates a staff review (continuationIn) or publishes a filing message to the NATS/STAN filer subject, and finally publishes an "PAID" email message to the emailer subject.

### Contract
- In: `POST` worker route in `resources/pay_filer.py` carrying a cloud event (`SimpleCloudEvent`) whose payload is a payment token (`status_code`, `corp_type_code`, `filing_identifier`, and the pay token used for lookup).
- DB: reads `filings` by `payment_id = :pay_token` (raw SQL, bound parameter); writes `payment_completion_date`, `payment_status_code`, `status`; writes a `Review` (staff review).
- Out: `queue.publish_json(subject, payload)` to `FILER_PUBLISH_OPTIONS["subject"]` with `create_filing_msg(filing.id)`; to `EMAIL_PUBLISH_OPTIONS["subject"]` with `create_email_msg(filing.id, filing.filing_type)` (option hardcoded "PAID"). Publishing uses STAN `publish` of a UTF-8 JSON payload.

### Decisions (pay_filer worker)
- `verify_gcp_jwt(request)` returns a message (falsy = OK); a message gives 403. It checks the Bearer token against audience `SUB_AUDIENCE`, then `email_verified` and `email == SUB_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`; any exception becomes an "Invalid token" message.
- Empty `request.data`, a non-`SimpleCloudEvent`, `status_code != "COMPLETED"`, or `corp_type_code in ["MHR","BTR"]` → 200, message dropped.
- Filing not found: if `filing_identifier is None` and `corp_type_code == "BC"` → 200 drop; otherwise 404 so the message is redelivered.
- `filing.payment_completion_date` already set → 200 drop (the only idempotency guard).
- Otherwise set completion date (UTC now), `payment_status_code="COMPLETED"`, `status=PAID`, `filing.save()`.
- `filing_type in ["continuationIn"]` → `create_staff_review(filing)`: Review status AWAITING_REVIEW, filing status AWAITING_REVIEW. Otherwise `publish_to_filer`, which publishes only if `filing.effective_date <= payment_completion_date` (future-dated filings are skipped here).
- Then `publish_to_emailer`.

### Boundaries
- Only the worker route is guarded (JWT above). `/healthz` and `/readyz` in `resources/ops.py` have no checks and do not test DB or queue. `create_app` only wires Sentry when `SENTRY_DSN` is truthy (config turns the literal "null" into "").
- The filing is saved (committed) before any publish. `create_staff_review`, `publish_to_filer` and `publish_to_emailer` all run under `suppress(Exception)`: failures are swallowed with no retry or record.
- `Filing.get_filing_by_payment_token` catches all exceptions, prints, and returns None. A DB error therefore looks like "filing not found" (404 → retry, or 200 drop in the BC/no-identifier case).
- `queue.py`: `publish_json` runs the async publish on `self.loop`, reconnects if not connected, logs and re-raises errors. No duplicate guard.
- The Filing/Review models here are minimal copies of the legal-api tables. `Review.save` has no validation. `BaseEnum`/`BaseMeta` in `utils/base.py` give `in` checks and `get_enum_by_value`.

### Hazards
1. After `filing.save()` marks the filing PAID, a failed filer publish is swallowed and the message is acked (200). The filing stays PAID but is never processed, and a redelivery is dropped by the `payment_completion_date` guard.
2. A DB read error in `get_filing_by_payment_token` is indistinguishable from "not found" and can silently drop BC no-identifier payments.
3. Future-dated filings are not published here. The notes do not show what picks them up later.

### Open first
- `resources/pay_filer.py`: the whole workflow and its drop/retry rules.
- `services/gcp_auth.py`: JWT check.
- `database/filings.py` and `database/review.py`: the models written to.
- `services/queue.py`: NATS/STAN publisher.

### Connections
- [L7] legal-api `reviews.py`: staff review decisions publish to the same emailer and filer subjects (filer only when APPROVED and effective date has passed). This is the downstream path for the AWAITING_REVIEW filings created here. The two sides must agree on the message shapes; the notes show no check here.
- [L1] legal-api `business_filings.py` `resubmit_filing_for_review` and [L12] legal-api `models/review.py`: legal-api moves the Review to RESUBMITTED. business-pay only creates the initial AWAITING_REVIEW review. Both sides share the `reviews` table and the `ReviewStatus` values.
- [L4] legal-api `models/filing.py`: the Filing status enum here mirrors it. The notes name CORRECTED, which legal-api derives from COMPLETED plus a completed parent.
- [L5], [L8] legal-api filing save and [L9] `publish_event`: other publishers to the filer queue with `{filing: {id}}`, the shape business-pay's `create_filing_msg` also targets (notes don't show its exact fields). Unlike L9, which swallows errors, `queue.publish_json` here re-raises, but the caller suppresses it.
- [L10]/[L11] read `BaseEnum`; [L2], [L3], [L6] are other services with similar names (`register_endpoints`, `publish_json`) and are not relevant.

## Role
The `pay_api.models` layer (SQLAlchemy ORM models, Marshmallow/cattrs schemas, query helpers) over the payment database. Services in pay-api, pay-queue and payment-jobs call its classmethod finders and savers. It calls no external services. It reads the current user via `user_context` (for `Audit`, `Comment`, `search_purchase_history`) and app config `LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE`.

## Contract
- In: plain Python calls with ids, status lists and `search_filter` dicts. Models are plain tables: invoices, payments, payment_accounts, cfs_accounts, routing_slips, refunds, statements, EFT tables, EJV tables, fee schedules, distribution codes and others.
- Out: ORM rows, or schema/DTO objects. `unstructure_schema_items` (utils/util.py) calls `schema.from_row` per row, then `converter.unstructure`. `InvoiceSearchModel` is used by CSO for reconciliation. `json_util` encodes Decimal as float.
- `models/__init__.py` registers `DBTracing.query_tracing` on the Engine `before_cursor_execute` event.

## Decisions
- `Invoice.update_invoices_for_revenue_updates`: PAID → UPDATE_REVENUE_ACCOUNT, REFUNDED → UPDATE_REVENUE_ACCOUNT_REFUND, then `bulk_save_objects` and commit.
- `Invoice.find_outstanding_invoices_for_account`: includes APPROVED or PARTIAL invoices. It also includes PAD invoices that are PAID and created on or after `from_date`. The EFT branch compares `payment_method_code` to `[APPROVED, OVERDUE]` (invoice statuses), so it is likely a bug.
- `Invoice.determine_overdue_date`: the 15th of the month two months after `created_on`, adjusted for America/Vancouver.
- `InvoiceSchema._clean_up`: drops CANCELLED line items, drops a business_identifier starting with 'T', and shows PAID as COMPLETED. `InvoiceSearchModel.from_row` applies the same T and PAID rules.
- `Payment.search_purchase_history` (user_context):
  - `return_all` False: paginates by a subquery.
  - `return_all` True with `max_no_records` > 0: limits the subquery.
  - Otherwise: more than 60000 rows raises `BusinessException(PAYMENT_SEARCH_TOO_MANY_RECORDS)`.
  - `filter`, `filter_payment`, `filter_corp_type` and `filter_date` build the criteria: `paymentMethod` NO_FEE means total == 0, and dates are converted to `LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE`.
  - `filter_details` is the line-item/JSON details search.
- `Payment.search_account_payments` and `find_payments_to_consolidate` use FAILED/CREATED, CC/PAD and consolidated-invoice subqueries.
- `PaymentTransaction.find_stale_records`: status not in COMPLETED/CANCELLED/FAILED, older than the cutoff, method CC or DIRECT_PAY. `find_active_by_*` requires status CREATED, and by invoice also an ACTIVE `InvoiceReference`.
- `InvoiceReference.find_by_invoice_id_and_status`: CANCELLED returns the latest by id desc; other statuses use `one_or_none`, which raises if there are several rows.
- `CfsAccount.find_effective_by_payment_method` returns accounts whose status is not INACTIVE. `find_effective_or_latest_by_payment_method` falls back to the latest.
- `RoutingSlip.generate_cas_receipt_number` appends 'L' for a child (`parent_number` set) and `R{n}` when `cas_version_suffix` > 1. `search` filters by number, status, amounts and so on, ordered by `created_on` desc.
- `RoutingSlip._add_receipt_number` matches `Payment.cheque_receipt_number` with method CASH (`receiptNumber`) or CHEQUE (`chequeReceiptNumber`).
- `Refund` has a check constraint: invoice_id or routing_slip_id must be set.
- `EFTCredit.get_eft_credits` uses `with_for_update()` and orders by `created_on` ascending; `remaining_amount` > 0 unless `include_zero_remaining`.
- Active-window rules (start ≤ today and end is null or ≥ today) live in `DistributionCode.find_*` and `FeeSchedule.find_all`. `FeeSchedule.find_by_filing_type_and_corp_type` and `StatementSettings.find_active_settings` use the same rule.
- `EFTShortnameLinks` active statuses are LINKED and PENDING.
- `Statement.StatementDTO.from_row` adds 8 hours to `to_date` when set.
- `CustomQuery.filter_boolean` raises ValueError on None. `filter_conditionally` skips None and uses `func.DATE` for dates.

## Boundaries
- None of the entry points has an authorization check. `search_purchase_history` uses `auth_account_id` and `user.product_code` only as filters.
- Writes: `bulk_save_links`, `bulk_save_recipients` and `update_invoices_for_revenue_updates` call `bulk_save_objects` then commit, with no try/except. `FeeSchedule.save` is `add` then commit. A failed commit is not recorded or retried here.
- No outbound calls. `CfsAccount.bank_account_number` is encrypted (key is `ACCOUNT_SECRET_KEY`, see L8); nothing handles a missing key.

## Hazards
- `Receipt.find_by_invoice_id_and_receipt_number`: `filter_by(receipt_number=...)` is not assigned back, so the receipt filter is silently ignored.
- `EFTRefund.__mapper_args__` has a reported syntax error (missing comma).
- The EFT branch in `find_outstanding_invoices_for_account` compares `payment_method_code` to invoice statuses, so it likely never matches. No duplicate guards exist, for example on `eft_short_name_links`, `ejv_link` or bulk saves.

## Open first
- `models/invoice.py`: status transitions, outstanding queries, `InvoiceSchema`.
- `models/payment.py`: search, purchase history, consolidation queries.
- `models/payment_transaction.py` and `models/invoice_reference.py`: active/stale transaction lookups.
- `models/routing_slip.py`: search and receipt numbering.

## Connections
- [L1] pay-queue `identifier_updater.py` calls `Invoice.find_by_business_identifier(old_identifier)`, sets `business_identifier` on each invoice, and commits once. It checks only that the message has 'tempidentifier'. The new identifier is not validated.
- [L2] payment-jobs `eft_task.py` reads `EFTShortnamesHistorical` and uses EFT services. The notes show no guards.
- [L11] `bcol_refund_confirmation_task.py` reads `InvoiceReference`/`Invoice`/`Payment` for BCOL refunds. It sets REFUNDED only when `invoice.total + bcol total == 0`; otherwise it reports to Sentry and skips.
- [L9] auth-api `user_context` is similar to the decorator that `Audit` and `Comment` use for user names. The notes do not show pay-api importing it.
- [L8] `ACCOUNT_SECRET_KEY` is the AES key behind the encrypted `bank_account_number`.
- [L10] `CfsAccountStatus` is an auth-web enum. Its PENDING and INACTIVE values match the statuses the CFS finders use. It also has PENDING_PAD_ACTIVATION, ACTIVE and FREEZE.
- [L12] payment-jobs `cfs_create_invoice_task.py` uses `InvoiceReference`, but the notes show no handler logic.
- [L4] DEVELOPER_NOTES describes the invoice foreign-key constraint and the Marshmallow-to-cattrs move.

## Role
The legal-api data-model layer for LEAR. It holds the `Filing` ORM model (filing lifecycle, status, fee-code and sub-type lookup tables), the `Configuration` key/value table (dissolution limits and cron schedules), and the `DCRevocationReason` enum (text for digital-credential revocation notices). `models/__init__.py` only re-exports these. It takes work from API resources, jobs and queue workers, which read and write these rows. It hands off to the DB through SQLAlchemy, with commits inside the model methods.

## Contract
- `Filing` rows are created and read by callers. `filing_json` carries `filing.header.name` (filing_type) and sub-type fields. `Filing.json` emits a header with date, filingId, name, status, deletionLocked, colinIds, comments, affectedFilings, isCorrected and isCorrectionPending. It adds effectiveDate, paymentStatusCode, paymentToken, submitter and paymentAccount only when present.
- `Configuration` rows (`name`, `val` as string) are read by name. The involuntary-dissolutions job reads the stage cron strings and NUM_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED.
- `DCRevocationReason` values are fixed message strings.
- Fee codes live in the filing-type tables by legal type and sub-type. `get_fee_code(legal_type, filing_type, filing_sub_type)` reads them: a sub-type uses `[sub]['codes'][legal_type]`, then a top-level `code`, then `codes[legal_type]`.

## Decisions
- `Filing.receive_before_change` (before_insert/update) sets `_status`, in this order:
  - skip when `skip_status_listener`.
  - skip when status is AWAITING_REVIEW, CHANGE_REQUESTED or REJECTED, or APPROVED with no `transaction_id`.
  - `lear_epoch` → EPOCH.
  - `transaction_id` → COMPLETED.
  - `payment_completion_date` or source COLIN → PAID.
  - `payment_token` → PENDING.
  - otherwise DRAFT.
- `block_filing_delete_listener_function` (before_delete) raises 403 'Deletion not allowed.' if `locked` or `deletion_locked`.
- `locked`: true if `deletion_locked`, or if a payment token was not added in history, or if `colin_event_ids` exist.
- `filing_json` setter: raises the lock exception if `locked` and not CHANGE_REQUESTED. If a `_payment_token` exists and the status is not CHANGE_REQUESTED, it validates against the rsbc_schemas 'filing' schema. On failure it clears `_filing_type` and the payment token and raises 422.
- `source` setter: 400 if the value is not in the `Source` values.
- `payment_completion_date` setter: 403 unless the filing is unlocked and has both `_payment_token` and `_filing_json`.
- `status` property: reports CORRECTED when `_status` is COMPLETED and the parent filing is COMPLETED.
- `delete()`: refuses if `locked`, otherwise deletes and commits.
- `set_review_decision(status)`: only CHANGE_REQUESTED, APPROVED or REJECTED are allowed, otherwise `BusinessException`. If APPROVED and `effective_date` is in the past, it sets it to now. It then saves and commits.
- `resubmit_filing_to_awaiting_review`: requires `_status == CHANGE_REQUESTED`. It sets the status and `resubmission_date`, then commits.
- `reset_filing_to_draft` calls `save()`, which commits.
- `set_processed`: sets `_completion_date`. It moves `effective_date` up to `payment_completion_date` unless the type is annualReport or changeOfDirectors and the business is CP or BEN.
- `legal_filings()`: returns None if there is no `filing_json`, otherwise the deep-copied segments whose keys are truthy in `Filing.FILINGS`.
- `Configuration.validate_configuration_value`, run on before_insert/update: the value must be a str. The NUM/MAX_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED names must parse as int >= 0. The STAGE_1/2/3 schedule names must pass `croniter.is_valid`. Failures raise ValueError to the caller.

## Boundaries
- No permission checks on any finder, `save`, or `Configuration` method. The only refusals are the lock, status and validation checks above.
- No duplicate guard and no retry on commit. `get_most_recent_legal_filing` and the other finders do not check that the business exists.
- `Filing.json` calls `ColinEventId.get_by_filing_id` and each `comment.json`. Any exception becomes a `KeyError`.

## Hazards
- `get_temp_reg_filing`: the filing_id filter is built but never chained to the query, so it ignores `filing_id`.
- `filing_json` schema validation and the status change are skipped while the filing is CHANGE_REQUESTED.
- `receive_before_change` can overwrite a manually set status, because its rules run on every insert and update. Only the skip cases above protect a status.

## Open first
- `models/filing.py`: status listeners, lock logic, review/resubmit steps, fee-code tables.
- `models/configuration.py`: dissolution config validation.
- `models/dc_revocation_reason.py`: notice texts.

## Connections
- [L1] involuntary-dissolutions job: reads `Configuration.find_by_name` for the stage cron strings. The model checks cron validity on write, so a bad cron cannot be saved. The job's own checks are not described in the notes.
- [L12] same job: creates Filing rows (DISSOLUTION / INVOLUNTARY) and publishes the filing id to the NATS filer subject. It uses `BatchProcessing`, which is not defined here.
- [L3] business-pay: has its own minimal Filing with a matching Status enum, and looks filings up by payment id. It does not go through this model's listeners.
- [L2] digital credentials worker: `DCRevocationReason` is the reason-text enum for its revocations. The notes do not show the link.
- [L4], [L5] UI: reference the restoration sub-type `limitedRestorationToFull`, which matches the fee table here (RESXF).
- [L6]–[L11] share only names (RegistrationBootstrap, BatchProcessing) and do not touch this part.

- `reset_filing_to_draft` calls `save()`, which commits.
- `set_processed`: sets `_completion_date`. It moves `effective_date` up to `payment_completion_date` unless the type is annualReport or changeOfDirectors and the business is CP or BEN.
- `legal_filings()`: returns None if there is no `filing_json`, otherwise the deep-copied segments whose keys are truthy in `Filing.FILINGS`.
- `Configuration.validate_configuration_value`, run on before_insert/update: the value must be a str. The NUM/MAX_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED names must parse as int >= 0. The STAGE_1/2/3 schedule names must pass `croniter.is_valid`. Failures raise ValueError to the caller.

- No permission checks on any finder, `save`, or `Configuration` method. The only refusals are the lock, status and validation checks above.
- No duplicate guard and no retry on commit. `get_most_recent_legal_filing` and the other finders do not check that the business exists.
- `Filing.json` calls `ColinEventId.get_by_filing_id` and each `comment.json`. Any exception becomes a `KeyError`.

## Hazards
- `get_temp_reg_filing`: the filing_id filter is built but never chained to the query, so it ignores `filing_id`.
- `filing_json` schema validation and the status change are skipped while the filing is CHANGE_REQUESTED.
- `receive_before_change` can overwrite a manually set status, because its rules run on every insert and update. Only the skip cases above protect a status.

## Role
Shared library (`entity_queue_common`) for LEAR NATS Streaming (STAN) queue services: builds/parses queue messages, runs the STAN subscriber with reconnect, exposes health probes and logging/Sentry setup. It takes messages from NATS/STAN and hands them to a service-supplied callback; it publishes JSON to STAN subjects. Used by entity-pay, entity-filer, entity-emailer, entity-bn.

Note: the `__init__.py` docstring ("Applies filings to the Business Database") is just a header; no code there.

## Contract
- Message shapes (`messages.py`): filing `{'filing': {'id'}}`; payment `{'paymentToken': {'id','statusCode'}}`; email `{'email': {'filingId','type','option'}}`.
- `publish_email_message(qsm, subject, filing, option)` awaits `qsm.service.publish(subject, payload)`. Callers: entity-filer (MRAS emails, option `'mras'`; filing status emails) and entity-pay (PAID).
- `ServiceWorker.publish(subject, msg)` → `sc.publish(subject, json.dumps(msg).encode('utf-8'))`.
- Inbound: `sc.subscribe(**subscription_options, cb=cb_handler)`; options merged from config `SUBSCRIPTION_OPTIONS`.
- `subscribe_to_queue(stan_client, subject, queue, durable_name, call_back)` calls `stan_client.subscribe(...)` and returns the subject; no validation or error handling.
- Exceptions (`service_utils/exceptions.py`): `QueueException` (base), `FilingException` (no filing matches payload), `EmailException` (no email processor matches).

## Decisions
- `get_filing_id_from_msg`, `get_data_from_msg`, `get_payment_id_from_msg`: on `AttributeError`, `NameError` or `JSONDecodeError` they return None.
- `get_data_from_msg` reads `list(token.values())[0][key]`, i.e. the first top-level key, whatever it is.
- `ServiceWorker.connect()`: if `not self.config` raises `AttributeError('missing configuration object.')`. Otherwise closes the old NATS client, creates new NATS and STAN, connects NATS, connects STAN with `conn_lost_cb`, then subscribes.
- `conn_lost_cb`: retries `connect()` up to 100 times, breaking on success. It logs and swallows each failure.
- `QueueServiceManager.run(loop, config, callback)`: creates the worker and Probes, starts the probe, connects, and registers SIGINT/SIGTERM → `signal_handler` → schedules `close`.
- `error_cb`: logs NATS errors. `signal_handler`: logs, then schedules `task()` on the loop.
- Probes: `healthz_handler` returns 200 only if components exist and every `await component.is_healthy` is truthy, else 503. `readyz_handler` does the same with `is_ready`. `meta_handler` reports component versions.
- `service_logger`: Sentry is initialised only if `SENTRY_DSN` is non-empty and not `'null'`. `before_breadcrumb` returns None, so no breadcrumbs are kept. Log level comes from `LOG_LEVEL`.

## Boundaries
- `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/meta`: no authentication; no timeout on component checks.
- `connect()` has no retry on the initial connect. Retry exists only in `conn_lost_cb`.
- `publish` has no idempotency guard and no retry.
- `run()` catches all exceptions after `probe.start()`, logs them, and does not re-raise or retry.
- `close()` swallows all exceptions (debug log). A `CancelledError` while closing the old NATS client is swallowed and `nc` is set to None.
- The messages module does no validation of identifier, type or option.

## Hazards
1. The `conn_lost_cb` loop gives up silently after 100 failed attempts. The worker is then left disconnected, while the probes can still report as configured.
2. The `run()` start-up failure is only logged. The process may stay up without a subscription.
3. The message parsers return None on malformed input, so callers must handle None. The notes show no common guard.

## Open first
- `service.py`: `ServiceWorker` connect/reconnect/publish and `QueueServiceManager.run`.
- `messages.py`: the message builders/parsers shared by all workers.
- `probes.py`: health and readiness logic.
- `service_utils/handlers.py` and `exceptions.py`: callbacks and the exception types.

## Connections
- [L2] business-pay `pay_filer.py`: its notes say it sends `create_email_msg` here with filing id and type. The handler checks `verify_gcp_jwt` (403 if falsy) and runs on GCP, not STAN. The link to this part's STAN code is thin.
- [L4], [L5] entity-filer `worker.py`: call `publish_email_message(qsm, EMAIL_PUBLISH_OPTIONS['subject'], filing, option)`. MRAS option for AMALGAMATIONAPPLICATION, CONTINUATIONIN and INCORPORATIONAPPLICATION. The caller catches exceptions, sends them to Sentry and swallows them; no retry. A lost email is only a Sentry message.
- [L7] entity-pay `worker.py`: sends the PAID email via `publish_email_message` after committing `payment_completion_date`. Failure goes to Sentry and does not stop the filing publish. The payment message shape comes from here, and it also carries `corpTypeCode`, which `create_payment_msg` does not produce.
- [L6] entity-filer `cb_subscription_handler`: re-raises `OperationalError` and `FilingException`, and swallows other exceptions, so those messages leave the queue. [L7] entity-pay, by contrast, absorbs `FilingException`. The two handlers treat the same exception differently.
- [L3] entity-emailer: raises `EmailException`/`QueueException` from this library; `cb_subscription_handler` needs the Flask app.
- [L9]–[L12] filing processors raise `QueueException` (missing section, business exists, no corp number). The entity-filer handler then swallows it, so the message is dropped.
- [L8] entity-bn passes a `QueueServiceManager` into its publish helper; the checks are not in the notes.
- [L1] entity-pay `q_cli.py` is a test publisher. It sends `{"paymentToken": {"id", "statusCode": "COMPLETED", "corpTypeCode"}}` to `entity.filings` with no validation.

- Probes: `healthz_handler` returns 200 only if components exist and every `await component.is_healthy` is truthy, else 503. `readyz_handler` does the same with `is_ready`. `meta_handler` reports component versions.
- `service_logger`: Sentry is initialised only if `SENTRY_DSN` is non-empty and not `'null'`. `before_breadcrumb` returns None, so no breadcrumbs are kept. Log level comes from `LOG_LEVEL`.

## Boundaries
- `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/meta`: no authentication; no timeout on component checks.
- `connect()` has no retry on the initial connect. Retry exists only in `conn_lost_cb`.
- `publish` has no idempotency guard and no retry.
- `run()` catches all exceptions after `probe.start()`, logs them, and does not re-raise or retry.
- `close()` swallows all exceptions (debug log). A `CancelledError` while closing the old NATS client is swallowed and `nc` is set to None.
- The messages module does no validation of identifier, type or option.

## Hazards
1. The `conn_lost_cb` loop gives up silently after 100 failed attempts. The worker is then left disconnected, while the probes can still report as configured.
2. The `run()` start-up failure is only logged. The process may stay up without a subscription.
3. The message parsers return None on malformed input, so callers must handle None. The notes show no common guard.

## Open first
- `service.py`: `ServiceWorker` connect/reconnect/publish and `QueueServiceManager.run`.
- `messages.py`: the message builders/parsers shared by all workers.
- `probes.py`: health and readiness logic.
- `service_utils/handlers.py` and `exceptions.py`: callbacks and the exception types.

## Connections
- [L2] business-pay `pay_filer.py`: its notes say it sends `create_email_msg` here with filing id and type. The handler checks `verify_gcp_jwt` (403 if falsy) and runs on GCP, not STAN. The link to this part's STAN code is thin.
- [L4], [L5] entity-filer `worker.py`: call `publish_email_message(qsm, EMAIL_PUBLISH_OPTIONS['subject'], filing, option)`. MRAS option for AMALGAMATIONAPPLICATION, CONTINUATIONIN and INCORPORATIONAPPLICATION. The caller catches exceptions, sends them to Sentry and swallows them; no retry. A lost email is only a Sentry message.
- [L7] entity-pay `worker.py`: sends the PAID email via `publish_email_message` after committing `payment_completion_date`. Failure goes to Sentry and does not stop the filing publish. The payment message shape comes from here, and it also carries `corpTypeCode`, which `create_payment_msg` does not produce.
- [L6] entity-filer `cb_subscription_handler`: re-raises `OperationalError` and `FilingException`, and swallows other exceptions, so those messages leave the queue. [L7] entity-pay, by contrast, absorbs `FilingException`. The two handlers treat the same exception differently.
- [L3] entity-emailer: raises `EmailException`/`QueueException` from this library; `cb_subscription_handler` needs the Flask app.
- [L9]–[L12] filing processors raise `QueueException` (missing section, business exists, no corp number). The entity-filer handler then swallows it, so the message is dropped.
- [L8] entity-bn passes a `QueueServiceManager` into its publish helper; the checks are not in the notes.
- [L1] entity-pay `q_cli.py` is a test publisher. It sends `{"paymentToken": {"id", "statusCode": "COMPLETED", "corpTypeCode"}}` to `entity.filings` with no validation.
